en: General Table of Contents for the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liaotang Yi,
Volume One:
Recorded Sayings at Yanqing Temple in the Prefecture of Qingyuan.
Recorded Sayings of the Guangdu Monastery on Mount Zituo, Taizhou Prefecture,
Volume Two;
Recorded Sayings of the Tianning Monastery, Qingyuan Prefecture.
Recorded Sayings, Verses on Ancient Cases,
Praises, and Self-Eulogies of Tiantong Temple,
Volume Three.
Postscript to Volume Four of the *Gāthā-saṃgraha-uddāna-kṣudra-buddha-kārya* (Verses on Minor Buddhist Rituals)
The Recorded Sayings of Master Liaotang, Volume One:
The Record of His First Residence at Yanqing Chan Temple in Qingyuan Road,
Compiled by His Disciples Zongyi and Shengduan.

In the first year of the Zhishun era (the Gengwu year), on the fourth day of the eighth month in autumn, the Master accepted an invitation at the Head Seat’s quarters in Wanshou Chan Temple in this province.
On the following day, he entered the temple and, pointing to the mountain gate, said: "Those with eyes upon the crown of their heads know before it is even raised;
when the water reaches the channel, the moon appears as the clouds part."
In the Buddha Hall, burn incense and say: "Before the birth of the Buddha, there was a singular and extraordinary matter;
this morning, it is presented face-to-face. Then, prostrate.
Occupying the hall, a bright mirror stands upon the dais. As things arrive, it reflects them all: the scaled fish leap amidst the waves, and the dull-witted birds nestle within the reeds.
Ascending the seat, he holds up the incense and says:

"This incense is offered specifically to pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! May Your Majesty, by the power of the Golden Wheel, govern..."

[The Emperor’s] longevity is equal to heaven and earth; the jade candlestick [of the world] is perfectly harmonized. His brilliance surpasses that of the sun and moon. Next, he picks up the incense and says: "If one smells it, it has no scent at all;
yet when used, it heats the earth and perfumes the heavens. People say its value is heavy within this Sahā world, but I say it is not worth a single coin.
I burn it in the incense burner as an offering to the former abbot of Jianyan Chan Temple in Pingjiang Road, Yangqi."
The eleventh generation: Venerable Zhu Yuandao. To repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk, he adjusted his robes and took his seat. The presiding monk struck the gavel and said:
"In this assembly of dragons and elephants at the Dharma banquet, you should contemplate the primary principle. The Master said: "Seek the wondrous before the movement of the mind."

Planting flowers in the sky; seeking the profound beneath words; grasping at the moon in water. If there were a true master among Zen practitioners, they would not hesitate to resolve doubts before the assembly.
A monk asked: "When one person rejoices, the myriad people depend on them. As a student who has come here, I ask the Master to offer a blessing."

[The Master] said: "The kalpa-stone may have a day of exhaustion, but the sovereign’s grace has no end. [The student] asked: "I have already received the Master’s instruction regarding the blessing of the Sovereign;
as for the matter of the Supreme Vehicle (zōngchéng), what is it like? The Master said: "Every pair of iron oxen has golden horns."
Jin said, "Blowing the holeless flute, its sound is heard throughout the world. The Master said, "Stretching out one's hand, one cannot see one's own palm.
Jin said, "If one does not ascend the tower to look out, how can one know the depth of the vast ocean? The Master said, "Diu Ba’s cloth shirt is worn through. Jin said, "..."
"If it is thus, then there is cause for gratitude. The Master said, "Upon the eight-flowered ball, there is no need to embroider the red banner.
The monk bowed. The Master then said: "Ceasing my travels to visit teachers of various quarters, I have returned to the ancient city of Modu.
With a dusty face and a head covered in ash, I dwell within these four walls; yet how can one avoid past karmic conditions? Thus, I have come to preside over this small Zen grove on the riverbank."
Water winds around a thousand villages; rafts span across the severed harbors. A few strokes of a soft oar, a single melody of a fisherman’s song.

Entrust this to another to truly proclaim and manifest—it is truly transcendent of emotion and beyond all description. Without cause, the Dharma drum is struck, and monks and laypeople arrive in throngs.
Yet you further wish for this mountain monk to add feet to a snake’s image. Faching spoke the Dharma before a clay statue; when the situation was urgent, he devised a plan. Fengxue alone...
In the seventh year of the Ding cycle, when cleverness is exhausted and clumsiness emerges, Fenyang plays the West River Lion with a divine head and ghostly face;

Yangqi plows the fields to earn his meal with an iron heart and stone entrails. This crew of ancient sages—whose worldly fame and wealth once perfumed the heavens—now puts on an air of bone-deep poverty.
Xinyanqing, however, is not like this: he raises his whisk, and all the stars in heaven bow toward it.
North. Among humans, there is no water that does not flow eastward. [The Master] speaks again: Zhaozhou, because a monk asked, "Does even a dog have Buddha-nature?
Zhaozhou said, "No. The Master says: "Zhaozhou’s 'dog has no Buddha-nature'—how many have misinterpreted this throughout ancient and modern times?
Since the unification of the Six Kingdoms, all is vast and tranquil; under the sun of non-action, the days of transformation grow long. The Head Monk addressed him.
Zhuī said: "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said:
"The wind does not rustle the branches; the rain does not break the clods of earth. Dongshan planted pines atop Diamond Ridge;
Guishan received the precepts within Guoqing Temple. The cuttlefish of the Eastern Sea and the bamboo shoots of the Southern Mountain—all are one's own self."
Buying and selling. He asked further, "How is it? [The Master] said, "A lacquer bucket is not fast. He struck the meditation seat and descended. Ascending the hall, he said:
"To erect the Dharma banner and establish the fundamental tenets—this is clearly the Buddha’s command at Caoxi.

Although Master Yongjia raised his staff and hoisted the banner of victory, it was much like stealing the bell while covering one's ears. With his whisk, he drew a line and said, "A bundle of willow—"
The silken thread cannot be gathered; it remains draped with mist upon the jade balustrade.
Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall: "The livelihood of a patch-robed monk is not much: let go of all conditions and proceed with leisurely steps.
The fire of three-stacked wood is warm and glowing; one does not realize the red sun has already risen in the east."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Zen Master Fenyang, who addressed the assembly, saying: "If you recognize the master’s staff, your journey as a wandering monk is complete.
Sanjiao said: "If you recognize the master’s staff, you will enter hell like a shot arrow. The Master said: "Both these venerable elders were pierced through by the staff.
At Yanqing, it is not so. Taking up the staff, he said: 'The winter is not yet cold; wait until after the twelfth lunar month to see.'"
A small *chán* (meditation) discourse on New Year’s Eve. A monk asked: “At the end of the year, when the night falls, there is a person who has not yet returned from ten thousand miles away.

What is this person who has not yet returned? The Master said: “His eyes are like drum mallets. The monk pressed further: “Who knows that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is another way of thinking?”

The Master said, "The *Biluo Stele* has no counterfeit wood. The student asked, "A single word cuts off the mouths of a thousand rivers; only atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak does one attain the profound.
The Master said, "Mistakenly identifying the zero point on the scale. Then he continued: "As soon as the winter solstice is seen, the year-end festival arrives once more.
The two luminaries race in haste; all things undergo transformation and succession. Transient life is like this—honor and decline, gain and loss—are but empty affairs."
It is all so confused! We, the śramaṇas and sons of the Śākya, are not pressed by hunger or cold, nor do we suffer the toil of conscription or corvée labor.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day and night, how should we conduct ourselves? To seek the profound and the mysterious is to waste one’s spirit;

to remain in non-action and non-activity, on the other hand, results in mere negligence. The Great Master Linji said: "There is a true person of no station who is constantly present before the faces of you all."
Entering and exiting through the gate. Those who have not yet attained realization, look! To speak in such a manner is like being exiled to the precipice of Wanzhou.
After a long silence: "Next year there will be new branches; the spring wind’s vexation shall never cease."
Again, it is cited: A monk asked Touzi, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there.
The monk asked again, "How far apart are the ordinary and the sage? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there. The Master said, "Great indeed is Touzi!"
Using official rank as a matter of personal favor; spoiling the salt and the vinegar; offenses reaching to the heavens. Entering the hall:
A rooster flies off with a lamp-bowl; a turtle blows on a fishing pole. A precious sword is cast into the void; divine light makes one’s gall bladder shiver.
(With his whisk, he draws a line. The Persian chews up three catties of coin. Do not seek it upon the head of Vajra.

Later, on the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall. Within the monastic community, as soon as people hear it said that the lantern and the pillar intersect, they immediately engage in extraordinary deliberations;
yet when it comes to ordinary conversation, they pass each other by right before their faces. [The Master] drew a stroke with his whisk.
This morning is the fifteenth day of the first month. Tonight, lanterns are lit everywhere. A lecture on the Buddha’s Birthday:
The Tathāgata’s birth occurred this very morning. Queen Māyā was his mother; pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, she spoke with such eloquence.
Having grasped the [true] meaning, he has been deceiving gods and scaring ghosts for two thousand years. Son!
How many of you descendants can truly know this? Yunmen’s decree was such that even a shrimp cannot leap out of its bucket.
Everyone vied to pour foul water over his head, causing the great earth, mountains, and rivers to run upside down.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What can be placed within the adamantine eye? The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment what could be placed there, what do you call the 'adamantine eye'? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Go ask the lantern.
The monk further asked, "How does one apply effort throughout the twelve periods of the day? The Master said, "There is no place for you to apply effort. The monk bowed.
The Master bowed and said: "I have been confined to my quarters by illness for a long time and have not ascended the hall. Yet, while speech has its intervals, this Dharma is without interval.
Day and night, I rely solely upon the myriad phenomena of the universe—walls, tiles, and pebbles—to expound it for the sake of the assembly.
Thus it is said: 'Dust speaks, lands speak, they speak with blazing intensity; all things of the three periods of time speak. [He struck the whisk. If you were to listen with your ears..."
In the end, it is difficult to meet; only when the eye-organ hears the sound does one truly encounter intimacy. (He lets out a shout. He addresses the assembly:
"A whisk made of tortoise hair and a staff of rabbit horn—take these up before others and let them measure them. Yesterday I went for a stroll through the village ahead;
every field is full of water and the fragrance of the rice flowers fills the air. (He strikes the whisk and descends from his seat.)
At the conclusion of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "I cite Master Cuiyan’s instruction to the assembly: 'During this summer, I have spoken with you monks here and there;
look at Cuiyan’s eyebrows—do they still remain? The Master said: 'Abundant wealth facilitates good trade; long sleeves facilitate a fine dance.
But when examined closely, it is like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled."

Ascending the hall, he cited the teachings: "When knowledge and views establish further knowing, that is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and views are without seeing, that is nirvana. He struck the meditation seat and said:
"Mundane affairs should be settled by the way of public justice; the human heart is difficult to align with the orb of the moon."

Offering Incense on the Anniversary of the Patriarch’s Memorial: Sitting coldly for nine years, he sold flour mixed with chaff; Carrying a single sandal in his hand, he sold a dog while hanging up a sheep.
On the fifth day of the tenth month every year, The descendants waste a great deal of incense upon him.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Yesterday there was one monk who came from Luofu, and another monk who came from Nanyue.

One had a long head and short legs; the other had a broad forehead and drooping brows. Both possessed the Dharma-body and mind. Now tell me, which of these two persons deserves the offerings of devas and humans?
He drew a stroke with his whisk. "The gibbons cry out in the gorges of Ba; the frosty moon is bright at dawn. He snapped his fingers once. *Pa*.
Why must the intestines wait for three sounds? The Buddha ascended the hall after attaining the Way. Śākyamuni was born in a royal palace; his nostrils—the great head—pointed downward.

He practiced austerities in the Snowy Mountains for six years; his nostrils—the great head—pointed downward. At night he beheld the morning star and awakened to the Way; his nostrils—his great head—pointed downward.
[The Master] faces downward. He strikes the whisk. "How many are these arbitrary circuit-inspectors? They do nothing but beat bricks and smash tiles.
On the occasion of the New Year’s Day lecture, he cites Chan Master Huanglong Nan: A monk asked, "The old year has passed and the new year has arrived;
without involving either of these two paths, I ask the Master for instruction. Huanglong said, "In the east, Jia-yi is wood. The Master says: This monk...
It is almost as if a scaled dragon leaping from the waves had suddenly emerged from within the eye of a needle;
yet, how could the Yellow Dragon fail to stir up a sky-reaching crimson flame from amidst a heap of cold ashes? Tell me: does this involve two paths, or does it not involve two paths?
Is there an indication, or is there no indication? [The Master] brandishes his staff and strikes once. General Li has a glorious reputation, yet he did not receive a fief.
This too is leisure.
Entering the hall, he said: "Yesterday, having returned from the city, an old farmer by the roadside invited me to rest for a while.

What I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears was nothing other than that which flows forth from the pure nature. Thus, I have composed a verse, which I shall now present to you all. [In] the small garden..."
Fresh ginger reveals its purple sprouts; beans climb the fence where half the flowers have withered. Children with hair tied in topknots stand barefoot in the mud;
having caught a glistening carp, they return home boasting of their catch. Then he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall: The first half of summer has already passed; before the hall, the iron saw dances its three stages. The second half of summer has not yet arrived;
the pupils in one’s eyes whistle and cry out from the wood. Now is midsummer: the monkey climbs the tree, tail trailing over its head.

Let the Five Ranks of Dongshan and the Three Mysteries of Linji be set aside for a moment. After long rain, the sun suddenly breaks through; everyone should take this opportunity to dry their leather and straw mats.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: The matters of the three-month summer retreat are now complete; so it has been for hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas.
A macaque smashes the mirror of Xuanyuan; a wildcat emerges from the grass, its horns pointing toward heaven.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "To have words and speech is all talk of worldly truth; to be without words and without speech is not yet the place where a patch-robed monk walks.
Fortunately, we are before an assembly of humans and devas; I pray the Master will grant us instruction. The Master said:

"A few sounds of the clear chime are beyond right and wrong; a single idle man dwells within heaven and earth. The monk stepped forward and said: "I ask specifically for this to be circulated. The Master said: "Without oil, there is no lamp."
[The Master] lights the lamp. The monks prostrate in thanks. The Master then says: "The myriad dharmas are the light of the mind; all conditions are but the clarity of one's nature.

Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened; it simply requires resolution this very day. The seven patriarchs of the Western Heaven and the two or three [patriarchs] of this land—all the old monks throughout the world—are but people who have not yet attained realization.
He strikes the whisk. "Where do the yellow leaves come as they drift with the water? The ox..."
"Cold crows pass through a neighboring village.
He ascends the hall, takes up his staff, gives a shout, and strikes the ground with the staff, saying, "Finished! Then he descends from the seat.
He ascends the hall again: "Bodhi, nirvana, suchness, and liberation—these are what all Buddhas have realized. Ignorance and afflictions—"
"Delusive thoughts and worldly toil are the karmic delusions of sentient beings. Consider this: before the world was formed, there were no names for Buddhas and no names for sentient beings.
Where, ultimately, could all these complications have been placed? After a long silence, he said: "Let the vast ocean change as it may; I shall never explain it for you."
The Recorded Sayings of the Chan Master of Guangdu Chan Temple on Mount Zituo, Taiding Prefecture, compiled by his disciples Siqi and Sijing.
On the first day of the tenth month in the winter of the second year of the Zhizheng era (the Renwu year), the Master entered the temple. Pointing to the mountain gate, he said:
Having entered this gate, do not harbor the notion of knowing or understanding. A clay ox barks at the moon; a wooden horse chases the wind.

At the Buddha Hall, while burning incense, it is said: "The hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are to be recognized upon the tip of a single hair. Although gold dust is precious, [it blinds those with eyes].

If it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. Occupying the room, I say: "This Dharma-seal of mine is spoken for the sake of benefiting the world. He raises his staff and says: "Thirty blows if you can speak;
thirty blows if you cannot speak. He strikes the staff down. A cart should not be pushed sideways; there is no crookedness in principle.
Severed.
Holding up the robe: at Mount Kukkutapāda, it became a case of doing something superfluous; at Huangmei in the middle of the night, it was all the more perceived as eccentric.
Today, at Tuo Peak, it is personally transmitted and received; when unfolded, it is neither too short nor too long.

The Monastery Decree: These are the words of the present sage-ruler and worthy minister, who secretly protect the Great Dharma. The Certification for Ordination states: "It is not improper to proclaim these before the assembly."
The commentaries of the various mountains of the Three Schools: speaking in silence, and being silent while speaking; calling a bell a jar, and proving a tortoise to be a turtle;
coral branches supporting the moon branch by branch.

A Brief Account of Rivers and Lakes: The mountains of Yue and the waters of Wu; spring trees and evening clouds. The majestic phoenix and the auspicious qilin naturally rise above the crowd. Pointing to the seat:

This is the precious seat of the Dharma-emptiness, upon which all may ascend together. Yet even Sumeru and King Lampa remain one degree below it. Ascending the seat, he holds up incense and offers this prayer:

The assembly rose from their seats. The Master adjusted his robes and took his place. Preceptor Husheng struck the gavel and said: "In this Dharma assembly, you dragons and elephants should contemplate the primary principle (*paramārtha*).
The Master said: "To have a question and an answer is still within the realm of ordinary sentiment; to be without affairs and without action is still to harbor cognitive understanding.
Is there anyone here who is uniquely liberated and without dependence? If so, let us meet. A monk stepped forward and asked: "What about Kunshan? (referring to Mount Kunlun).

[The Master] said, "Pàn Kěnxiào’s Hall: the Seal of Returning to the Source has long been personally transmitted. Today, Tàofēng celebrates the Emperor and opens the hall; I pray to hear the essential Dharma.
The Master said, "Striking the golden bell atop Mount Sumeru. The student asked, "A single phrase that transcends past and present, loftily treading upon the crown of Vairocana.
The Master said, "I do not strike this drum or blow this flute. The student asked, "What is it? The Master said, "It is not that there is no sound; it is simply that there is no one to hear it."

[The student] asked: "In the past, when Baoshou opened the hall, Sansheng threw his body across [to assist him]; when Linji took up residence at a monastery, Puhua exerted all his strength to support him.
Ultimately, what did they clarify? The Master said: "Both ends are completely severed; a single sword leans against the sky, cold. [The student] further asked:
"If so, then the five ranks of ruler and subject are all torn asunder, and the weapons of the three mysteries are withdrawn at once."

The Master said, "To apply names and words is an error. A monk let out a shout, bowed, and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "These confused Chan practitioners are as numerous as hemp and millet.
Then he said: "When I press my finger, the Sea-Seal emits light; before the hall of the ancient Buddhas, one knocks at emptiness seeking a sound.
'It is not the wind or the banner that move; it is the mind of the wise man that moves. On the road to Caoxi, one gouges sores into healthy flesh. Directly—
Even if one were to have a separate livelihood, it would still be nothing more than mixing mud with water. Today, at the newly expanded monastery, the hall is opened for the sake of the nation;
after all, what matter should be discussed? New Ra and Jambudvīpa clash forehead to forehead; the lantern and the pillar intersect.
The wisdom of all wisdom is pure, without duality, without division, without distinction, and without interruption. It is exactly thus.
At that time, let us speak: what rank does this phrase behind the head occupy? After a long silence, he said: "Take well a single unperforated flute;
casually blow forth the joy of ten thousand years. He further cited: A monk once asked Jia Shan, "What is the realm of Jia Shan?
Shan replied, "A monkey carries its young back into the green peaks; a bird holds a flower in its beak before the azure cliffs. Fa Yan said:
For twenty years, I understood this only as an objective realm. The Master said, "Jiashan let go too extravagantly; Fayan brought it back too frugally.

When examined closely, neither has yet found a way out. Venerable Husheng struck the gavel again and said, "Contemplate carefully the Dharma of the Dharma-King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma-King."

That evening, during the informal sermon (*xiaochan*), a monk asked: "If one attains realization before words, it is still being stuck in the shell of delusion; if one takes responsibility based on a phrase, one cannot avoid becoming obstructed wherever one goes.
As a student who has come here, I ask the Master for a skillful means. The Master said: "A sleeping cat beneath a peony flower. The monk stepped forward and said:
"As for the words in the *shu* (the formal discourse), not only are the phenomena and principle perfectly integrated, but I am also glad that the Master..."
"How is it when the conditions for meeting [the Way] are fulfilled? The Master said, "The iron saw dances three times before the hall.

The student asked, "In that case, the green mountains do not lock the soaring momentum; the vast ocean surely knows its source is high. The Master said, "The great elephant of Jia Prefecture eats too much salt;
the iron ox of Shan Prefecture becomes even thirstier. He then said, "Within the jurisdiction of Anzhou lies Mount Zituo."
Preface. This monastery was formerly the site where Chan Master Hunyuan Mi and successive generations of renowned virtuous ones proclaimed the Way;

it is truly a field of enlightenment in the southeast and a vast reservoir for the dragon-elephants [of the Sangha]. A person as unworthy as I has been honored by the command of the monastery to succeed to the seat upon this mountain—a great privilege indeed.
I rely on the presence of the Elder Abbot, my late teacher, above me; I humbly pray that his longevity may equal that of Zhaozhou, so that he may endure forever.
The life-force of the Buddhas and Patriarchs has been fulfilled through my inquiries both morning and evening; this is a most great fortune.

Nevertheless, regarding the "small-scale sermons" (xiaocan) of the monastic groves—what are called "family instructions"—I have not yet had the leisure to examine such matters as the size of the cauldrons or the length of the ladle handles.
I am confident that this assembly of ours is like refined gold from a hundred smeltings or well-trained fine steeds; they transcend the ordinary and require no further elaboration.
He further composed another verse and presented it to the assembly: "The crescent moon atop the bamboo hat peaks half a thousand li; The many scholars travel together, undaunted by the toil.
For now, let the master staff rest against the wall, And behold together the myriad ridges rising like billowing waves."

The Head Seat and the Librarian, Xie, ascend the hall. The Eye of the Human and Heavenly Eyes, the Head Seat within the Hall—within the sphere of those who have attained penetration, one knows before the words are even raised.
Whether it be the Great Canon or the Minor Canon, whether fully presented or partially presented, what is this but the sound of a hot bowl clinking?
The green vines wind their way straight up to the crest of the cold pine; the white clouds, pale and limpid, appear and vanish amidst the vast emptiness. (He strikes the whisk.)

The master descended from his seat and ascended the hall. He raised the precedent of Mingzhao’s instruction to the assembly, saying: "The wind here is somewhat harsh; let us return to a warm place to deliberate.
The assembly followed him to the abbot’s quarters. Mingzhao said, "As soon as you reach a warm place, you fall asleep," and with his staff, he struck them all at once.
[The Master] dispersed the assembly. The Master said: "Old Mingzhao cast out a single pivot; it was indeed extraordinary.
At that time, had the entire assembly been keen and discerning monks, as soon as he said, 'For now, let us go to a warm place to deliberate,' they should have all departed at once."
Teaching the One-Eyed Dragon: there is reason that cannot be fully extended.
Descend from the seat. Ascend the hall. At night, the rope does not move; one suspects it is a snake. The dark room is fundamentally empty; one fears there are ghosts.
One loses the sword in the Kunming Pool, yet finds the saw upon the banks of the Qujiang River. A-he-he! La-la-li! The wagtail.
"The tongue is three thousand li long.
He ascended the hall and said: "In this way, in this way—if you grasp it within the mind, even *eranda* (Ilan) becomes a sandalwood tree.
Not in this way, not in this way—if you miss the essential meaning, even nectar becomes a garden of thorns. [He then] recited praises atop the bell tower from his seat.
"Planting vegetables underfoot. Chief Seat Sheng said, "A fierce tiger sits in the middle of the road. [The Master asked,] "And what about that? He struck his whisk and descended from the seat.

At the Winter Solstice, during the small *paramārtha* (small *chán*), a monk asked: "A single grain of elixir can transform iron into gold; a single word of ultimate truth can transform the mundane..."
He attained sainthood. A student came forward and requested, "I ask the Master for a single point. The Master said, "The head is long and the feet are short.
The student pressed further, "As for when a monk asked an ancient worthy, 'What is the matter of winter coming? and the worthy replied, 'The capital produces great yellow [radix]—what about that?
The Master said, "A gold coin covers the tongue. The student pressed further, "For those of initial resolve and junior students who have newly entered the monastic groves..."
"Is there not, however, a skillful means? The Master said: "The scale-weight and the saw cut through; blood flows profusely. He then said:

"The scriptures state that the Dharma is beyond seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing. If one acts within seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing, this is merely seeing, hearing, perceiving, and knowing—it is not the seeking of the Dharma.
The heavens revolve to the left and the earth turns to the right; the sun rises in the east and the moon sets in the west; cold comes and heat goes; yin reaches its extreme."
The yang is born; the iron tree blooms; the icy river erupts in flame. The Way of the gentleman flourishes;
the Way of the petty man wanes. Can you call this seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing? Or can you not call it seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing?
To understand it in such a way is precisely to mistake the dust for the head. Therefore it is said: "If one lets go, the Tathāgata radiates light; if one holds fast, there is only mud and sand."
Concealing his brilliance, he raised his staff and said: "The wild landscape is not cut off by mountains; the light of heaven connects directly with the water. He ascended the hall and said:
"In deep mountains and rocky cliffs there is no Buddha-dharma. Stones are large or small; for one winter and two winters, hands are folded across the chest.
Blowing a pipe at the edge of the fence is originally just the wind from last night."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: One day, while Zhaozhou was on the well-tower, he saw Nanquan passing by.
He clasped the pillar with his hands and cried out, "Save me! Nanquan struck the pillar five times with his staff and departed. Zhaozhou then immediately assumed the full ceremonial regalia.
He went to the Abbot’s quarters and thanked him, saying, "I have just come to thank the Master for saving me. The Master said, "The sword that kills is the sword that gives life.
On New Year's Eve, he gave a small *can* (sermon), saying: "In one year there are three hundred and sixty days. Tonight, the year ends and the cycle is exhausted.

While other places discourse on the wondrous and talk of the profound, here we respond to the times and receive blessings. From the Seven Patriarchs of the Western Heaven to the Two Ancestors of this Land, the old masters throughout the world..."
"Upādhyāya, you are always one who strikes clean balls and embraces a child that does not cry.

For example, though lutes, harps, and *kōng-hou* zithers possess wondrous sounds, if there are no skillful fingers, they can never produce them. Within the realm of the patch-robed monk, it does not lie in manifold complexities.
The earth is frozen and the heavens are cold; I pray you, take care. He further raised the case: A monk asked an ancient worthy, "When the year is exhausted and the age..."

He skillfully employed expedient means, yet he could only say half the truth, and then descended from his seat.

When West Hall Master Yuan went up to the hall for the formal teaching, he overturned the banner pole in front of the gate; the elder brother called and the younger brother responded, but for a long time no sound was heard.

Upon the Buddha’s path, he ascends the dais: he leaves the city to renounce the world, draws his sword to cut off his hair, and for six years on the Snowy Mountains, fills his hunger with hemp and wheat.
At night, beholding the morning star, he achieves supreme enlightenment. *Sha!* The wind and moon of Chang’an pierce through past and present—what man is this?
The child crawls along the wall.
The Abbot and the Rector ascend to the Dharma Hall. The Abbot Xian stands facing Inspector Li with his body turned slightly to the side; when the water reaches it, the channel forms naturally.
Kebin the Rector was defeated in the battle of dharma and received a staff-blow and a fine. The clouds part and the moon appears; he uses the whisk.
The Son drew a single line. A stone ox blocks the ancient path; one horse gives birth to three tigers. On New Year’s Eve, the small *paramārtha* assembly:
it is like the earth supporting a mountain, yet unaware of the mountain’s towering loftiness; like a stone containing jade, yet unaware of the jade’s flawlessness.
It cannot be known through intellect, nor recognized through consciousness; it cannot be constructed through words or language.

It cannot be understood through silent stillness alone. Throughout the year of three hundred and sixty days, every person daily enters the Sangha hall and the Buddha hall, offering incense and tending the fire, drinking when thirsty and eating when hungry, speaking or remaining silent, rejoicing or becoming angry—whatever various activities they perform, how could there ever be a lack?
When the year reaches its end and the time is exhausted, hearing the sound of the drum, they ascend to the Dharma Hall like wild geese.
Walking and standing—what is one trying to depict? This mountain monk occupies this curved wooden chair, speaking of yellow and black, pointing east and drawing west;
this too is like painting a snake and adding feet. Suddenly, he brandishes his staff and strikes once:
a winter melon hung upon a gourd vine, honeyed fruit suspended from a Huangbo tree. He then raised another case: The Great Master Huineng addressed the assembly, saying: "I..."
"There is an object that has no head and no tail, no name and no character, no back and no face. Do you all recognize it?
At that time, Heze Shenhui stepped forward and said, "This is the fundamental source of all Buddhas; it is the Buddha-nature of Shenhui.
The Patriarch then struck him with a staff and said, "If even calling it 'an object' is not appropriate, how much less so [to call it] the 'fundamental source' or 'Buddha-nature'! This...
The disciple turned away. [The Master said: "Even if one were to cover one's head with thatch grass, one would still only become a follower of the school of intellectual understanding.

The Master continued: "Who can resolve the myriad functions in the presence of the sun? Everyone vies to confound others with their intellectual needles and awls. The wooden man holds the board and strikes it amidst the clouds;
the stone woman holds the flute and blows it beneath the water."
Ascending the Dharma Hall on the first day of the year and the beginning of spring, he addressed the two orders: "A hundred years are hard to find for the dawn of spring;
One immediately perceives the new气象 (qi-xiang) of heaven and earth. The clay ox at the bottom of the sea battles until its horns are broken; The iron hawk atop the peak dances as it turns its body.
You masters of the granaries, officials of integrity and purity, And leaders of the monastic community, men of virtue and character— May you offer blessings of boundless longevity."
The Sage’s Life. A single burner of aloeswood incense swirls in dense clouds.
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascends the hall and says: "A monk asked Zhaozhou, 'When one lamp lights hundreds of thousands of lamps, from where does that original lamp originate?
Zhaozhou leaped out with a single sandal. Furthermore, he said: 'An adept would not ask in such a manner. The Master [concludes].
He said: "The first arrow is still light, but the second arrow is deep. Nevertheless, you must see from what place a single lamp is ignited;
even so, it is not yet sufficient. He struck the whisk.
Returning to the hall from within the city, an ancient worthy said: "The royal officials bind one with painful constraints; the Buddha-Dharma does not circulate.
He held up his staff and said, "Tell me, the duck’s leg is naturally short, and the crane’s leg is naturally long—what of it?
He struck the ground with the staff: "The spirit tree in the village of three households; the stone *gandang* at the crossroads."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade; Creek water is as clear as indigo. Every thing is entirely true wisdom— What need is there to point it out further?
Three before, three after, three and three. How pitiful that old man of Vaiśālī in days of yore Allowed only Mañjuśrī to converse with him."
The Head Seat of the Double Grove (Śāla Grove) ascends the hall. Great Master Fu, together with the Seven Buddhas, practices the Way atop Mount Yunhuang.
In a dream, Yangshan sees the Second Seat preaching the Dharma in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace. Two arise from one; even one cannot be clung to.
All day long, all is vast and empty; what matter can hinder it? Suddenly grasping the staff, he strikes once. "When the ground of the mind does not give rise [to thoughts]..."
Idle grasses and trees. Naturally, his body emits white light from between his brows.

On the occasion of the Buddha’s birthday, he ascends the hall and says: "When the World-Honored One was first born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, walked seven steps, and looked around in the four directions, saying:
'In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am the most honored. [The Master] picks up his staff and asks: And tell me—"
"Is the Master’s staff the same as or different from Śākyamuni Buddha? Holding up his staff, he said, "Kuan! He then ascended the hall and, citing Layman Pang, said:
"In daily affairs there is no difference; only I myself am in harmony. At every turn there is neither grasping nor rejecting;
in every place there is no discord. Who designates 'red' and 'purple'? Mountains and hills are free of even a speck of dust. Spiritual powers and..."

"Sublime function: carrying water and hauling firewood. The Master said, "When Layman Pang speaks in this manner, those throughout past and present who have attained thorough realization are as numerous as hemp and millet;
those throughout past and present who have misunderstood are as numerous as hemp and millet. He then drew a line with his whisk.
Asuras hold the sun and moon in their palms; the golden tortoise bears Mount Sumeru on its back.
Entering the hall, a monk asked: "When Vimalakīrti remained silent, he was treading his own private path; how does the Master proclaim it for us? The Master said:
The monk said, "In that case, there is one emerging and one submerging. The Master said, "A lantern hanging on the water. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "You wild-rice-gatherer!
The monk said, "Do not say that you do not meet anyone. The Master said, "Wrong. Then he said: "The Buddhas realize great nirvana;
sentient beings wander through birth and death. Taking up what belongs to the Buddhas, [I] present it before the faces of sentient beings."
Can it be done? Can one take that which belongs to sentient beings and place it before the Buddhas? Yet, the Buddhas and sentient beings are neither one nor two.
To reach this point, one must first attain clear understanding. (He struck the whisk and descended from the seat.)
Ascending the hall: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, the mouth of the cloth bag is tied shut; a thousand soldiers are easy to find.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the mouth of the cloth bag is untied; a single general is hard to seek. Now tell me: how do you speak that phrase which neither ties nor unties?

Small-scale Sermon upon the Resolution of the Summer Retreat: Among the hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable subtle meanings, seek only within yourself; do not seek them from others.
Therefore, the Great Master Linji said: "The light of the pure mind in a single thought-moment is the Dharma-body Buddha within your own house."
The light of the mind of non-discrimination in a single thought is the Sambhogakāya Buddha within your own house;
the light of the mind of non-distinction in a single thought is the Nirmāṇakāya Buddha within your own house. To see it thus is to melt jars, basins, hairpins, and bracelets into a single gold.
Churning the cream, curd, and clarified butter into a single flavor: before the Hall of the Bright Moon, it is always midsummer;
beneath the Gate of the Great Sun, every day is the third autumn. Who cares for you whether it be long-term or short-term? To cultivate mindfulness and gather the mind—what is there to say?
Is it the "goose-guarding-snow" or the "candleman-in-ice"? Or the iron ball? Although this is so, if you sit inside a grain basket and remain hungry...
"A dead man! A dead man submerged head-deep in water, dying of thirst. What more can one blame him for? [The Master] brandishes his staff and strikes once.

Thus, this summer has passed in vain. I do not dare hope that the Master will preach the Buddha-Dharma;

it would suffice for me merely to hear the two characters of the "True Cause" (zhengyin). Upon hearing this, the Elder said, "Disciple, do not speak so hastily. If one speaks of the True Cause, there is not even a single character.
Having said this, he tapped his teeth and remarked, "I was not right to have spoken thus just now. An old man was heard from the next room.
An old master once said, "It is a pity that a single pot of soup has been defiled by two mouse droppings.
The Master said, "This old master did not speak with the monks for an entire summer, yet at the very end he says there is not even a single word of the 'True Cause.

“Mòyǎn! After a long silence, he said: ‘If you do not enter the surging waves, how can you manifest yourself as a man who sports in the tide?
He ascended the hall and said: ‘When the eye responds, it is like the thousand suns; the myriad phenomena cannot escape their shadows and forms. When the ear responds, it is like a deep valley;

there is no sound, great or small, that is not fully accommodated. He took up his staff and said: ‘The entire Tripitaka of the Buddhist teachings cannot equal its explanation. Only one who attains this [realization]—’”

Moxi has come from the West; he is one who provides proof. Holding up the staff: "The noble youth of the nine avenues is accustomed to wandering among the flowers; the impoverished scholar who has not yet passed the examinations has much cause for lamentation."
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, Master Xie ascended the hall and said: "It is not Zen, it is not the Way; searching north, south, east, and west is but a waste of effort.
Last night the sun’s orb shed osmanthus blossoms; this morning from the moon’s cavern grew magical mushrooms. A-he-he! Is it good? Is it not?"
Both the holy and the ordinary are cast down together. A rhinoceros breaks through the fan; seek the rhinoceros. The old woman’s heart is urgent; so it was with the Old Man of Yanguan.
When the Head Seat ascended to the hall, he cited how Master Dahui, while serving as Head Seat at Yunju, once went to Xixi...

Jizhuang encountered a monk who had arrived briefly from Yuantong. The monk asked, "I have not yet spoken of my realization; why do you say it is not? Dahui shook his head repeatedly.

This is like an old calendar; the Elder Miaoxi shook his head again and again, saying, "You go, you go;
it is not so. It is like adding mud to dirt. Suddenly, he seized his staff and struck once—*niú*.

The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining the Way: For six years he practiced austerities in the Snowy Mountains; without cause, he painted a tiger and ended up with a wildcat.

The practitioner shaves his hair; a single cap remains upon his crown. This was not transmitted by a thousand sages. To clear away weeds before the Hall is, in effect, to act quite arbitrarily.

A Minor Sermon for the Eve of the Year’s End. The most spiritual beings in heaven and earth still require a leap month every three years to perfect their work.
This year has comprised three hundred and ninety days; it is now precisely the night of ultimate completion. I cannot help but share a brief word with you, my fellow practitioners.
Deshan once addressed the assembly, saying: "Tonight I shall not answer questions. Should anyone come forward to ask a question, they shall receive thirty blows. At that time, a monk stepped forth.
The monk prostrated. Baizhang struck him. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; why do you strike me? Baizhang said, "What kind of person are you?
The monk said, "A man from Silla. Baizhang said, "Before you have even stepped onto the ship's railing, you deserve thirty blows.
Had Zhushan been that monk, at that moment, when he heard [Baizhang] say, "Tonight I will not answer questions," he would have asked a question.

"Thirty blows! I shall overturn the meditation seat! Thus, not only did he spare this old fellow from muddling through his confusion—mistaking the bell for a jar—but he also opened a path for the monks of the world to manifest their own true nature.
Tell me, by what principle was he able to act in such a way? He took up his staff: "The mechanism was not made by Han Guang; do not take it to heart."
While folding his robe, he spontaneously composed another verse: "What is the daily life of a patch-robed monk? The sun and moon race on, and yet another year passes.
All phenomena have always been fundamentally empty and still; The ocean of three thousand worlds is but a single reed hut."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Yangshan asked Muzhou, "What is the dwelling place of the true Buddha?
Muzhou replied, "By means of the wondrousness of no-thought, one turns back to contemplate the inexhaustibility of the spiritual flame. When thought is exhausted, one returns to the source;

nature and characteristics are eternally present, and phenomena and principle are non-dual—the true Buddha is thusness. Under these words, Yangshan attained sudden enlightenment. The Master said, "How great was Muzhou!"

He mistakenly applied conventional names and phrases to the true dwelling place of the Buddha, where there is no point of contact at all. Yangshan attained sudden enlightenment upon hearing these words;
it was much like mistaking a donkey’s saddle bridge for his father’s chin. [The Master] gave a shout.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "In spring, one sows a single seed; in autumn, one harvests ten thousand grains. There is no idle field in the four seas, yet farmers still die of hunger.
We, the śramaṇas and sons of Śākya, eat when hungry and seek coolness when hot. Do not say that this comes from cultivation in past kalpas, for it does not begin today.
After a long silence, he said: "If the great ocean were to know contentment, the hundred rivers would surely flow backward."

A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: For ninety days there is no labor spent in vain; a black ox lies dead in stagnant water. A hundred kalpas are contained within the function of the present moment;
a mangy horse is tied to a withered post. In the West, they take a wax man as their test—when one dog barks at the void.
In the East, they take an iron ball as their test—when a thousand monkeys gnaw at the reality. Yet they do not realize that, within the sphere of the patch-robed monk, it is like striking...
A spark from flint, a flash of lightning—whether you grasp it or fail to grasp it, you cannot avoid losing your body and forfeiting your life.
Even so, this is still but the rippling waves when there is no wind; you must further know that there is a path beyond this. [The Master] picks up his staff.
[He] sets the staff aside leaning against the wall. "Dry the straw sandals in the autumn wind."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddha-dharma is omnipresent in all places. Yet, in no place can the Buddha-dharma be subjected to conceptual deliberation.
He took up his staff and said: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. "When the ancients attained sudden enlightenment beneath these words, what was it like?
He struck the ground with his staff: "Where the power of Yu did not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west."

Ascending the hall for the conclusion of the summer retreat: Before the fifteenth day, the retreat is entered but not concluded; after the fifteenth day, it is concluded but not entered. On the fifteenth day itself, it is both entered and concluded.

"Ordinary people truly say it exists; those of the Two Vehicles analyze it and say it does not exist; Bodhisattvas say that its very substance is emptiness.

Seeking the blue sky upon the earth.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: the four seasons shift and pass; in the blink of an eye, all is changed.

Only now do we see the fire-clouds scorching the azure heavens, and again encounter the vermilion cassia falling in the autumn wind. Holding up his staff, he said: "Most look toward the heavens for the bright moon, unaware that they themselves are within it."
Guanghan Palace. Ascending the hall, he said:

The vast sky is of one color. Opening the furnace, I ascend the hall: those who have left the household life do so solely to investigate the Heart-essence school. The sun and moon race on in haste through summer and winter;
pay no heed to the heavy cold of the myriad mountains. In the earthen stove, firewood crackles until the night glows crimson. [He raises his staff: "The Bodhisattva Without Supernatural Powers."
How difficult it is to find his traces! Relying on his staff, he descends from the seat.
To offer incense for the anniversary of the Patriarch’s passing: Upon the Hall of King Liang, his mouth was full of frost; before the Peak of Shaoshi, he knitted his brows as he tasted the vinegar.
Incense clouds arise. Night is dark, day is bright. From the Western Heaven to the Eastern Land. Ascending the hall:
To speak with sufficiency is to speak all day long and exhaust the Way; to speak without sufficiency is to speak all day long and exhaust phenomena.
With his whisk, he draws a single stroke—the ultimate limit of both the Way and phenomena. With a single stroke, it is severed. On the banks of King Chu’s city, you—

This mountain monk has resided here amidst the deep clouds for thirteen years, and together with the great assembly, we have encountered this most auspicious season. All...

yet, for the most part, people remain stuck within the armor of "non-action. Consider, for instance, when Dōngshān was eating fruit with Chief Seat Tàiyuán:

Please remain and listen. I cannot avoid troubling you, Master Staff-bearer; let me explain it clearly for you. [He] struck the staff and again composed a verse, presenting it to the assembly:

Iron trees sprinkle flowers across the ancient ravine; Empty space provides a laugh that fills the donkey’s cheeks.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Good Wealth has entered deeply into the Vairocana Pavilion; Śakra has ascended high into the Hall of Good Dharma. At the peak of Mount Zituo, the sun stands at its zenith;

Small Lecture on the Eve of the New Year. Thanking the Head Seat and the Rector. The old year has ended; the new year is about to arrive.

At the summit of ten-thousand-fathom peaks, the ice is withered and the snow is ancient. Having nothing to share with the great assembly for the year’s end, I cannot avoid cooking rice from iron nails and soup from wooden slips.

"The vast universe holds countless people; how many know gratitude and understand how to repay it?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Below the mountain, the heat is like that in a steamer; within the mountains, the coolness is like autumn.

We should retreat from external pursuits and turn toward ourselves to investigate and clarify that one phrase which has not been transmitted by the thousand sages. Thus it is said: 'To offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land'—this is precisely..."
This is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
[The Master] ascended the hall and cited Dongshan Wushan’s address to the assembly: "A hundred-fold refined gold is used to cast an iron ox;

The Patriarchal Hall. From the Western Heaven to the Eastern Land, the flames of the lineage continue in a fragrant succession. Not entangled with the common or the sage, one who transcends these is called a Patriarch (*zu*).

Pointing to the seat, he said, "I shall not prostrate again to Sumeru-dīpa-rāja; I shall now ascend this seat.

The First Principle. A monk stepped forward and asked: "Seeking pearls in red water is still but a treasure of the human world; singing it forth amidst the clouds is certainly not a device beyond the ordinary.
