In the Qingxin Hall, noble aspirations remain far removed from the dust and dregs of the world. Deep within the clouds, this empty hall is constructed; the water is clear, and the rocks lie in rugged heaps. The moon is white, and the mountains are a vast, misty azure.

On the *qí* trees, autumn shadows fall; among the *yáo* grasses, extraordinary fragrances arise. Sitting alone beneath the four eaves in stillness, the celestial breeze penetrates with a subtle coolness.
Ten thousand cares do not reach one another; a single sheet of ice and frost remains solid. In human life, it is precious to know when to stop; years and months race like sails driven by the wind.
Who can endure the bitter toil of oil and flame, placing oneself in the arena of fame and profit?
The Daoist Goulong constantly recited the three characters "Hūṃ Hūṃ Bèi" from his mouth. I have composed this to present to the Daoist, saying:

"Recite 'Hūṃ Hūṃ Bèi'—how truly strange is the sudden emptiness of words and meaning! If you are a lion cub that startles the crowd, how exhilarating it would be to penetrate the point before the trigger!
How wondrous is this Way, which is utterly free of intimacy or distance; yet I fear you may still be clinging to what you have known before.
As for the conscious spirit: even if you were to empty the three periods of time in a single thought, you would still be one of those aimlessly feeling an elephant in the dark.
If you had not met the old Master Huanglong, how could you have known that common stones are not the ultimate treasure?

At that time, the gates of his teeth were not yet closed; both parties entered the wild weeds with their whole bodies. Identity within difference, and difference within identity—the transmission has never been easy to penetrate. Last night...
The clay ox fights its way into the sea; at daybreak, the iron hawk dances across the void.
To the junior attendant Simin, who was re-visiting Master Xuechuang of Yuyang:
On Mount Mao there is a master of the Way whose swift faculty is like a flash of lightning. He forges the sages and melts the common folk with his three-foot bamboo staff.
If you wish to pursue and re-enter this study, your resolve must be fierce and intense. Before your eyes, affairs are manifold; with one stroke of the sword, they must be severed in two.
When the venerable Shaoyang was alive, how could there ever have been any words or explanations? To transcribe them from a paper robe is merely to add more grit to the eyes.
I, an old man atop Tal Peak, am a hundredfold ugly and a thousandfold clumsy. As you depart, you seek words of parting; I have but one mouth and no double-tongued speech.

This numinous light is inherently present within yourself; you must simply gaze directly until it penetrates through and through. Should you remain in a state of half-presence and half-forgetfulness, I fear there will never come a time of realization.

In the same rhyme, I present this gift to the monk Yù: In our school, we discuss the Real, not the empty. A hair’s breadth of deviation, and heaven and earth are divided. Clouds rise from the Southern Mountain, rain falls on the Northern Mountain;

the neighbor to the east makes a horse, the neighbor to the west makes a donkey. With the rivers and seas as one's tongue, the Dharma is difficult to expound; with iron and stone for one's entrails, kindness remains steadfast.
Not yet orphaned. Traveling at night is not permitted; you must arrive by dawn. Who would have known there was yet another red-bearded barbarian?
Next, the Reverend Dongzhou answers in the rhyme of the Reverend Gulin’s original manuscript:
“The Śūnyatā-deva stirs up evil, stubbornly boring through empty space. The wooden horse gallops, its four hooves unshod; the clay ox—”

Startled, he snapped off two horns; how does this compare to Fengtai and Huqiu? Towering above the forest of monasteries as a lofty peak, disciples flocked to him like water rushing down or clouds gathering.

His swift mechanism resounded like thunder and flashed like lightning; right before their eyes, he smashed the sand bowl to pieces, and auspicious mists and radiant light surged into the azure heavens.
A Gift to Elder Mida Yū: The Ultimate Way is without difficulty;
it is only that one dislikes making distinctions. Mountains are high and seas are deep; crows are black and cranes are white.

If you are a monk with the true eye, you will naturally transcend the school and surpass conventional standards. Vast kalpas do not consume even a single instant; what "ancient" or "present" could there be? There is none.

The entire boundary lies within a single speck of dust; it is neither broad nor narrow. Since the monastic forests possess such extraordinary talent that stands out from the crowd, why worry that one’s reputation will not shine resplendently?
Rubbing my aging eyes before the green peaks, I wish to behold the wings of the nine-thousand-li soaring phoenixes.
The Lotus Sutra transcribed in blood by Attendant Tao bears the title *Miaolianhua*.
It is the true secret essence of the Tathāgata; through skillful means, it unfolds the Three Vehicles. These words are not uttered by ordinary tongues.
The practitioner’s application is especially intimate; they exhaust the very blood from their mother-born fingertips. Upon a single hair-tip, spiritual power is revealed;
even across ten billion hair-tips, there is no difference. Beyond praise, beyond reach of joy. The assembly on Vulture Peak remains as it was.
One must take care not to let a speck of dust enter the eye.
Presented to Secretary T’ien-yüan Ta: In his youth, Dajue relied upon Yuantong; master and guest were in perfect accord, restoring our school. These words are neither identical nor separate;
like the high-suspended sun of wisdom, they enlighten the masses. Yuantong’s Way was so great that he moved the Son of Heaven; it is truly because of Dajue that this came to pass.
A man of talent under heaven; a minor messenger with silver seals to distribute imperial edicts. He elevates the worthy to replace himself—rare indeed is one like him.

With profound talent and far-reaching intellect from antiquity to the present, he adorns the ancestral vehicle (the Dharma) as a true connoisseur of its sound. This son of man exerts his will to surpass the ancients;
his golden resonance and jade vibration shall be transmitted throughout the monastic forests.
The ancient masters of Xianyan Huarock Eong were noble in their mutual accord of mind-to-mind; they did not forget the ocean of their compassionate vows when entering the world.

At every monastery, the waves of their grace have spread, and their radiant reputation remains vibrant to this day. Misreading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, I recall Master An; how can the Chinese and Sanskrit terms ever [be reconciled]?
It is relevant. Not only is there no Buddha, but there is also no self. In the blazing heat of the sixth month, ice and frost are cold.

The spirit and bearing of the Way-man are naturally distinct; he personally plucks the bright pearl from the dragon’s jaw. An old ancestor’s single broken sand-pot—turned upside down and held crosswise, he transcends all by himself.
In the same rhyme, I send off Attendant Zhen to travel among the masters:
it is simply that there is no teacher, not that there is no Chan. To "sever nails and cut iron" is but a mistaken interpretation and an erroneous transmission.

If one claims to transcend the present and surpass the ancients, the moment the mouth opens, one has already fallen into defeat. To further say there is a separate way of life is to throw sand and scatter earth right in one's face.

Even if one were to fit the great trichiliocosm into a single speck of dust and strike the third watch at midday, it would still be fitting to press them until their faces turn red, so they might know the true doctrine of Shaoshi.
If Cuiyan had not obtained the attendant Shanshi, how could he have clarified the ultimate reality and distinguished it from inert emptiness?

He traveled throughout the south and north of the Yangtze; you must know that he did not rely on the power of another. With a single thought, turning the light back within, one sees the intimacy [of reality].
Thus, Bodhidharma sat facing the wall for nine years in vain.
In the same rhyme, I present this tribute to the Chief Steward Cheng, who upholds the lofty command. He deceives the Hu and mocks the Han; he transcends the sages and surpasses the mundane.

Like thunder crashing and lightning flashing, he is like Xinghua striking Kebin or Fengxue meeting Nanyuan—his functional mastery spans the distance between heaven and abyss. Who could say his transmission is the same as others? Even were it Lingyuan himself...

Profound stillness is free from all dilution; how can my school be merely called "transmission and maintenance"? To point to an anthill as Mount Taihua, or to mistake a puddle in a hoofprint for the Abode of the Waters (Guixu);
to suffer cold while facing a blazing furnace, or to endure hunger while sitting amidst a basket of rice—such are the ways of the world.

A man of spirit must resolve to follow a teacher for definitive discernment; in this Way, do not deceive yourself. The life in Jambudvīpa is a swirl of clamor and agitation; in the blink of an eye, it becomes...
In his declining years, he sent the monk Donggang Xin as a secretary to reside at Tiangong Temple.
Old Nan met Ciming; Liangsu questioned Magu, who picked up an iron caltrop and smashed a flawless jade.

Having first roamed the Garden of Teachings, the golden probe has already been applied to my eyes; having returned late to the Forest of Chan, the golden arrowhead has further been drawn from behind my head.
It is not within that which is silent and still, for the pure model returns again and again; it is not without that which is vast and expansive, for the true pattern repeats itself.
I draw from the profound clarity of the twin ponds and follow the continuous flow of the great twin streams. May you universally bestow the rain of Dharma without delay;
infinite parched lands await your moistening and nourishment.

Zongyuan’s title is "Expanding the School and Broadening the Origin. He reviles the Buddhas and scorns the Patriarchs; he traces the current to find its source and, mounting his horse, beholds the road. There is not a single trace to be found, yet it is precisely here that one should investigate to the utmost.

Amidst the thousand differences and myriad distinctions, the eight thoroughfares and seven passages, one does not tread upon the tracks of those who came before—how could one then manifest the positions of those who follow?
Fierce flames melt ice; a sudden clap of thunder shatters a pillar.
The Head Seat Zhu Tanrui of Tiantai named his private quarters the "World of the Four Flowers" and requested a gāthā to certify it.
Boundless lands are fundamentally pure; why single out the Western Paradise? Sentient beings, with their deluded perceptions, sink into the sea of existence;

how vast and boundless are the waves of emotion and consciousness! In this Sahā world, Śākyamuni Buddha spreads his universal compassion, expounding the Dharma through many gateways according to the capacities of beings.
Through the sixteen meditations and the wheel of vows, one faces Amitābha and returns as a child to the Father. The pond of eight virtues opens...
There are four kinds of colored flowers. The ground is strewn with golden sand as large as chariot wheels, which is perfectly level without any slope.
It is exquisitely fragrant, pure, and radiates brilliant light. The Tiantai practitioner Zhu Tanrui used these four flowers to name his quarters, transcending mere words and meanings:
the Utpala, the Kumuda, the Puṣkara, and the Puṇḍarīka. He practiced walking meditation, sitting, and reclining amidst them, floating [in tranquility].
When myriad thoughts arise, they melt like spring ice. Vimalakīrti did not forget to cultivate the Pure Land; he clearly knew that the Buddha-land has been empty from the beginning.

In my school, where the path is solitary and perilous, what is there to accept or reject? When questioned, the painful staff strikes along with the voice. The white moon shines over the vast ocean as the mud-bull roars;
the wind rises across the great wilderness as the wooden horse neighs. Within a single hair-tip, one penetrates the ten voids; to carve out boundaries and limits is but a vain effort.
In this humble effort, having cast aside the "wind-borne" screen-mountain, one need not hinder Panlang from riding his donkey backward.
To the attendant Zhuang:
do not admire the various sages, nor prize your own spiritual essence. Your faculty is like a flash of lightning; your eye is like a shooting star. Strike and sing in tandem.
There is a standard. The meeting between teacher and disciple is no small matter. When the wild duck flew past, he let Baizhang off;
when the Minister attained realization, he did not strike Sanping. Piercing the mark before the sound, pulling out the nail from behind the head—he cast his iron net across Mount Tai and Mount Hua.
To capture the qilin in the vast blue ocean—how many deluded ones run about outside! With ears pricked high and hair disheveled, I present this to the Japanese Abbot Shunzō:
the direct pointing of the single transmission.
In the state of non-action where all learning is severed, the ocean of the Flower Treasury is instantly emptied; one brushes past the Vairocana Teacher and enters the immeasurable.

The Dharma-gate is entirely within you; throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas, it does not depart from this very moment. If you apply it in reverse and employ it in an inverted manner, you will see through the teaching;
even Deshan and Linji can still be pursued.

Manifesting the purity of the treasury, it rolls forth with clarity and vastness; yet to conceive of it in the mind is already to become bound. Upon the tip of a single hair, one recognizes the source;

the eighty thousand Dharma gates are suddenly revealed in their full breadth. "Is" and "is not," "right" and "not right"—these are merely the intellectual interpretations used to exhaustively probe the profound mystery.
Huanglong brings forth the severed rope of the underworld; only then do the tigers of meaning from the two rivers know where to return. The initial spark and the final application:
to cure an illness, one need not rely on medicine carried by a donkey. The *maṇi* jewel within the treasury has existed from of old; how radiant are the sun and moon at the edge of heaven!

He demonstrated that the treasury of liberation reaches the state where there is nothing to seek; that study reaches the state where there is nothing further to learn. Whether saint or ordinary person, all are brought entirely under his command.
The seventy-two ridges of the Qinyang River flow far into the eastern ocean; the eighteen-thousand-fathom Mount Tiantai rises as high as the Southern Peak. Rejoicing that there is a path—
It can be practiced. Laughing at being bound by no ropes, the ocean-treasury of Vairocana is overturned; turning one's head, one may well clip the horns of the azure dragon.
In the same rhyme, presented to Attendant Chu.

Producing aphorisms that reach the ultimate point—how many people throughout past and present have raised them? The meaning of the Tathāgata’s Zen and the patriarchs’ intent is, for the most part, difficult to transmit to those who are not worthy vessels.
The World-Honored Śākyamuni explained it in detail to Ānanda; the wheel of the correct and the inverted rests upon his golden arm.
It is not a matter of pursuing or investigating; lift your eyes and you have already traveled three thousand miles.
Guishan merely herds the water buffalo, needing no three-foot whip in his hand. Sons of noble spirit, do not delay in seeking the Way. Last night, the golden wind arose in the jade palace.

In the same rhyme, a gift to Attendant Shou, the "Lao-dao Yunmen" known as Nianqi: Receiving the resonance and inheriting the void has continued unto this day. When you pick up the seven, you lose the one.
To wield the adze, one must first possess the wood to be shaped. Kāśyapa’s clarity was never hidden; only now do I believe the Tathāgata’s words.
Not esoteric. This is a nest of old, first-rate entanglements. Why trouble yourself to bring it up again before the assembly?
To you, the cub of the golden-maned lion, a single blow from the top of the head is most appropriate. The ancestral domain is lofty and profound, not easily reached;

wishing to achieve great wisdom, one must first become a fool. Under the assembly of Linji was the crimson-tailed carp—who would say that a thousand errors are worth a single truth? At the very end...
Had he not met Old Jia-shan, he would have turned his body and leaped into the surging waves.
Presented to Attendant Juehai Chengyuan of Zhongzhu:
His nature-heaven is brilliantly radiant; it is ever-quiescent while illuminating, and ever-illuminating while quiescent. He holds his black staff upside down.

He waves his hand across the face. Who would have known he was so intentionally opening up his heart? Look! When the World-Honored One held up a single flower, the golden-haired *dhūta* monk alone smiled.
He merely beat the earthen drum and sang a rustic song; look at him, capable of producing a melody as refined as the "Yangchun" tune.
There is giving forth and there is gathering back; rising by himself, he falls back by himself.
In the same rhyme as "The Song of the Silent Hermitage," presented to Weiwaina:
From our school, there has never been a word or phrase; The golden gong and jade response—how could they differ? The old Śūnyatā-jīvaka sits in meditation amidst the crags;
The Flower-Rain Deva seeks him in vain. The Persian from the Southern Sea blows his iron flute; The mud ox turns its ear to listen.

Truly so! Amidst the clamor of those seeking the subtle and investigating the profound, how many can withstand a blow from my evil fist? Shaking out their skirts and robes, they remain ignorant of the truth;
without cause, the Great Sword is held upside down. Flames erupt from the icy river, shimmering of their own accord; blossoms fall upon withered wood, yet they vainly display their fragrance.
Do not allow them to dwell within the den of the heroic spirit; one must directly surge eastward and then submerge westward. *Gāthā* (Verse).
Having finished writing, I lean against the precarious balustrade. The heavenly wind grinds out the very bones of the azure cliffs.
Yu Shi’s Inscription: "The attendant Jie requested the Master’s inscription.
His resolve for the Way is firmer than stone; his stone-like firmness is as precious as a flawless jade gem. A skilled artisan carves and polishes it, yet the stone itself remains unmarred."
Firm! With firm resolve, the Way may be pursued to its profoundest depths. Be lofty and seek it within yourself; do not strive in vain for it on other mountains.
When Master Sengsheng preached the Dharma, [the statue] nodded its head; the five hundred laborers exerted their strength in vain.
In the same rhyme, I present this gift to Attendant Run:
The Eastern Land is separated from the Western Heaven; why should it hinder the secret transmission? To seek the subtle and pursue the profound is like learning the gait of Tang at Handan.
Every single thing is seen before one; every dharma forms a mutual discrepancy. The old barbarian Dharmatrāta was originally not the Patriarch.
When Shen Guang sought peace of mind, his coming intent never matched [the Master's response]. Examine it from the beginning: five times five is twenty-five.
Tending the furnace, one can indeed avoid neither fire nor heat. Who says that those on the same path travel by different tracks?

Behold him sitting with bare hands at the heavy barrier; how could he ever allow a single drop of water to leak through? With a single turn of the pivot before the time of Vipaśyin, he picks up a dead snake that is vividly alive.
Rolling forth from among a million people, his natural function is inherently extraordinary. This brings to mind Mount Jinluan.
O good attendant, Cuiyan personally suffered a crushing blow. Had he not encountered the venerable Ciming at that time, who would have cleared his heart of grievance?
Presented to Attendant Deng of Japan.
Attendant Xianglin Yuan has long been within the chamber of Shao Yang. Shao Yang’s Way does not involve verbal explanations;
yet this paper robe was transmitted recklessly, misleading those Zen practitioners who merely mimic the words and further aggravating their chronic addiction to the mists and clouds.

When one can breathe freely and move the body, casting aside the "seven and three" to preserve the "one"—at that moment of advancing beyond the hundred-foot pole, the sun rises upon the *bo-sang* tree.
Huzhi replied in the rhyme of his Dharma-nephew, Elder Kang of Longhua Muan:
"The stream of Chan practitioners from the four seas flows in every direction; the lineage of Shaoshi awaits one to uphold it. The true heir of Nantang is Fengtai."

The grandson’s ground is narrow, yet he excels at the long-sleeved dance. His swift mechanism lets out a single shout like a rolling thunderclap, seeking to open the true eye at the crown of the head.
The parched and withered shall surely be universally moistened; the Yellow River, with its nine bends, comes from Kunlun.

Following the calligraphy of Master Luoyue Ying, with wisdom that precedes and transcends fixed notions, one naturally empties the dreams of worldly toil. As the staff and shouts fly back and forth, the Dharma-gate is established;
it directly causes one’s courage to fail and the soul to tremble. From beneath the tongue of Miaoxi, winds and thunder roll, turning base metal into the elixir of gold.
Nine turns. What has the Daoist Luoyue studied? The horse’s head is north, the ox’s head is south. What I speak is like a timely rain;
you must listen with your ears plugged. From antiquity to the present, the flames continue and the fragrance links; yet among Buddhas and Patriarchs, not a single dharma has ever been transmitted.
A Verse in Response to the Abbot Zangzhu’s Departure for Further Study under Master Jitan at Zhongzhu Temple;
Not Yet Understanding Three Eights and Nine. It is difficult to tread the path of the Ancient Sovereign. The white jade is found when the stone is split; the blue sky is sought when the earth is dug.
This medicine has been gathered and brought here: pick up a single blade of grass. If you grasp the intent before the movement of the mind, what doubt can there be?

This is suspicious. To clarify the essential tenet beyond all measures—this is not something one should like, yet one likes it. Within this thicket of entanglements of five thousand-plus scrolls, the Ten Sages and Three Worthies have all been brought to their knees.
If you wish to become a true descendant of Deshan and Linji, you must further go to question the old man before Thousand-Year Rock.
Using this rhyme, I send it to West Hall Master Daocun:

The patriarchal style of Jibei and the Dharma-way of Jiangxi flash like lightning and roll like thunder, leaving nothing concealed; even the eyes of dragons and hawks find it difficult to investigate.
He whips up the stone *qilin*, and the venomous snake leaps from the grass in alarm; he bites through the iron *suānrào*, and the ten thousand phenomena are all at once revealed.
Praised as excellent, the mud-vajra causes sweat to flow; how could one hope to topple a snow-lion?
With spiritual acumen penetrating through to before the time of Vīraśabda, the autumn light fades upon the celestial fragrance of the cassia blossoms.
Mount Shan was titled En, and the head monk was titled Ruo-shan.
"Shan" (Mountain) is the essence of suchness (*tathatā*): above, it towers before the myriad phenomena; below, its roots penetrate to the bottom of the nine abysses.

The Great Spirit’s power is so vast it has nowhere to be applied; how could the Foolish Duke shift these mountains after so many years? The wind-whipped old trees transform into sharks and crocodiles;
the cloud-shrouded strange rocks crouch like bears and tigers. One might say the mountain is comparable to great grace, yet the Way is so vast it cannot be permitted to be expressed in words.
A three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves; the ice and frost lie in profusion across the entire universe.
The *Lotus Sūtra* Diagram: At the Deer Park, the celestial drum resounds;

for the Dharma Master, auspicious signs appear and radiant light unfolds atop Vulture Peak. Proclaiming the wondrous Dharma to awaken the multitudes, the three turnings and seven parables are how intimate!

The hundred realms and thousand suchnesses are fundamentally interpenetrating. Furthermore, heavenly flowers rain down in fragrant profusion, pervading the universe like the reflections in Indra’s net.
Layer upon layer, he returns the hand that upholds the school at the Deer Park; both ordinary beings and sages alike return within the Sea-Seal Samādhi.

The illusory chamber is temporarily occupied, yet the Real does not linger therein; delusion is fundamentally empty. As for this chamber named "Temporarily Occupied Illusion," what is it ultimately like? Within the shadow of a city in the sky, golden coins fly.
O Feng! Within the flash of a stone-light, one beholds the Brahma-abode; taking the emptiness of forms as its doors and windows, and establishing the barrier of the dharma of non-abiding.
Do not, upon hearing my words, give rise to doubt or wonder; the three realms are all equally a dwelling within a single dream.

Wandering through the sight of the Great Star and the Giant Spirit—since what year did they apply their axes and chisels? The cliffs and precipices rise steeply toward the azure heavens; the Milky Way stretches across like a neighboring wall.
The verdant peaks encircle one another like attending guests. At the fifth watch, the sun first appears from beneath the sea; in the third month, one does not yet perceive the people [of the world].
In the springtime, hidden radiance nurtures excellence within this ancient reservoir. Master Ji and Master Guan are like the phoenix and the qilin among monks.
Responding to Master Fangyan Dalin (II):
The banner of pride and the net of doubt have already melted away like ice; how far indeed is the Buddha-land from the palace of Māra? One should joyfully uphold the lion’s staff.
A mouthful of hemp rope is tied around Master Lü’s waist; a round jade mirror of one chi in diameter encompasses a thousand li. Six knots on his flowered headcloth form but a single strand.
Whether employed or set aside, he practices the Dharma of peace and joy. To those in lowly positions, who would say he is not as lofty as the high heavens?

The luminous perfection of the awakened nature—what manner of thing is it? To the ordinary it is not less; to the sage it is not more. How could a single piece of gold be hindered by being cast into a well?
Why labor with the parable of the three animals crossing the river? A precious sword hurls itself back into the air; let a dull blade be ground upon stone as it pleases.
Yongjia long ago failed to maintain his silence; yet the Song of Realizing the Way is still transmitted through ancient and modern times.
Reply in the Rhyme of the Letter Sent by Master Nantang (II):
For ten thousand ages, the lofty peak of Shaoshi remains; who can again summon the wind of the nine-year retreat? The Buddha’s illness and the Patriarchs’ illness are not in vain;

how could there be no penetration of the essence and penetration of the teaching? The marbled leopard knows only to hide in the mist and rain; the painted phoenix ultimately will not accept [the trap].
From the cage of worldly confinement, he skillfully draws the "blow-to-the-hair" sword from his sleeve to sever all manifold distinctions and reach the Great Sameness.
Casting away the worn axe upon the peaks of Lake Shang, he dwells in leisure while vigorously reviving the ancient ancestral style.

Not only does the sleeping tiger retain its full majesty, but there is yet another point of spiritual penetration like a luminous horn. Sitting through the night, sandalwood incense floats from the precious censer; at the dawn meal, water chestnuts and lotus roots fill the bowl.
The bamboo basket. The auspicious qilin snaps the golden chain; who can share its emergence from beyond the heavens?

In response to Master Huiweng’s verse on "Long-time Guests Ascending Junzi Peak Together": Moonlight over the river fills the hall, with the fragrance of cassia flowers in the breeze. The passage of years easily chases away the stars and frost.

A transformation: The meaning of the Patriarchs is difficult to convey through speech or silence. To bind a tiger, one must directly enter the tiger’s den; to raise a chicken, why necessarily shut it in a coop?
When the myriad functions have ceased and the hair on one's head is white as snow, the zither reaches the state of no strings, and its resonance is naturally in harmony.
Yantou and Xueqiao stayed at Aofeng; they shook out their very hearts and livers, revealing no trace of wind.

Having brushed past the Three Mysteries and the Five Ranks, they swept away secret realization and hidden penetration. How could a fine steed wait for the shadow of a golden whip? How could a phoenix be confined within an iron net?
At West Hill under the Great Ancestor, the many descendants share a family style that is naturally identical without being constrained.
Following the rhyme of Master Mengtang, I present this verse to the attendant Chang of Guoqing upon his second visit.
Having attained realization through his practice, the attendant has penetrated to the depths of the great kalpa before Vīraṇa. He wields the whip as iron horses race their course;

he strikes a scorched brick against the very bottom of the frozen river. Clearly knowing that there is fundamentally no Buddha outside the mind, he yet insists that within the alchemical elixir jar there is something else.
There is a heavenly being. When Bai Zhang first encountered the old story, he took empty space as his mouth, yet could not fully raise the challenge.
Next, following the rhyme of Master Shiwu’s Miscellaneous Verses (V):
"Much of this floating life is but a forced imitation; let go of emotional attachments and the Way can be mapped. Cloud shadows and stream reflections enter with clarity."

Seated, I offer fresh bracken shoots and *gomo* rice to the kitchen. Do not say that the spring flowers find it difficult to age; one should know that even at the age of childhood, the hair at the temples will soon wither.
All things, throughout ancient and modern times, undergo a chaotic transformation; none can escape the great furnace of heaven and earth.
This aged man has retired from all affairs in recent years; yet for their sake, I still move with idle worries.
The forests and springs are most excellent for wandering and play, but the sun and moon rush on, impossible to detain. To become a Buddha, why need one be born in the land of Zhuguo?
Most who achieve immortality merely long for Mount Penglai. One must reach the state of non-action from conditioned existence; how many can perfect the practice to reach the ultimate end?
Ants climb the living terrace upon empty steps; the red sun has reached three poles before the gate finally opens.

Shaking out my skirt and robe, I have no words to speak; carrying my flask and staff, a monk arrives. After the rain, viewing the waterfall is truly wonderful; under the moon, hearing the gibbons is all the more mournful.
The crane’s leg is naturally long and the duck’s leg naturally short—who was it that joined them, and who was it that cut them?

Those who aspire to the Way with single-minded sincerity and seek to resolve their doubts should act like a player on a chessboard during a match of victory or defeat. To perfectly realize Prajñā, one must empty the mind and its consciousness;

yet when fundamental ignorance establishes views and knowledge, it is as if one were naturally meant to seek pearls by casting oneself into the dark waters of the Chi River. How many instead gather pebbles from the spring pond?
Autumn clouds fill the eyes and one repeatedly scratches one’s head; it is precisely at this time that the Garden of Awakening lies desolate.
The myriad transformations hasten toward their end without ceasing; I am too weary to employ great elixirs to arrest my declining years.

Just as the frost falls and the river maples turn crimson, once more I see spring return and the wild fires turn green. For the Buddhas I carry a bowl of raw iron; for drawing water, who would use an ancient bronze pitcher?
A gust of celestial wind stirs the pine waves into a roar; with my pillow high against the southern window, I awaken from my midday nap.
Presented to Master Junshang:
Extraordinary matters from before his birth as a Buddha need not be sought outside of the present moment. With reed-sails he departed far from the banks of the Wu city;
with an iron staff he traveled eastward to the shores beyond the sea. Advancing alone, he came clad in the three robes of a mendicant; turning his head, he must cherish these two [feet].
Stem and brows: A new golden ball freshly emerged from the red furnace, startling a white phoenix down from the edge of heaven.
Answering Zongsheng Shouzuo:
Brothers, north and south, we have all become old men; when will we open our hearts to discuss this school? The original, inherent fountain-source is ever serene.

Profound! The manifestation of the mysterious Dharma is naturally layered upon layered. To see, you must let go of the moon and cease observing the finger; to hear, it is best to turn toward the hearing-mind rather than vainly strike the bell.
If we speak according to the Gate of the Patch-robed Monk, thirty blows of the black staff will not be lightly spared.

In response: Master Yuangming of Tiandong has vigorously expounded the principles of our school before the Nine Ridges; he is impartial toward Dangyang, neither partial nor biased. His brilliance surges forth from his own treasury of light, piercing through the "silent illumination" Chan of other houses.
While the learned interpretations of the sages vie for praise, he takes pity on those of us at the end of the tradition; his spiritual mechanism is uniquely liberated, inspiring all who admire him.
The former sages said: "I, an old man of mist and clouds, atop a thousand peaks, am delighted to see that the *Zhengzhuan* (Correct Transmission) exists at Shuangxi.

Entrusted to the Head Seat Zhongdu, the threads of the school’s lineage were about to fall to the ground, yet now they have found a cause to rise again. Through the profound interplay of 'knocking' and 'singing,' he hoped for those of transcendent capacity; indeed, his excellence has spontaneously met the needs of the times."
Distinct! At the place where the tea ladle leaps, the story is renewed. Beings everywhere cast themselves into the net of delusion; the sages in every dust mote ride the wheel of their vows.
Grasping the tip of a hair, wind and rain come with swift ease; the udumbara flower blooms, yet does not interfere with spring.

A Gift to Master Zhuang: The Eighteen Visions of Zhaozhou Regarding Nanquan. The Mind-Seal has no transmission; this is the true transmission. The wooden horse neighs in alarm, newly freed from its halter;
The iron ox sleeps soundly, long since forgotten the whip. His twin eyes flash like lightning, impossible to peer through; His mouth holds frost as he speaks.
It remains whole. "The moon in the empty realm over the azure pool for ten thousand ages—what prevents it from shattering the heavens within the water?
A response in the rhyme of Master Yinjun Xuanyi (II).
"The warm glow of crimson clouds bathes people in intoxication; waters wind around level slopes, and bamboos surround the hermitage. The Way reaches the ultimate mystery and is fundamentally..."
2. Teaching according to names and signs, the three divisions: Snowflakes float upon the bowl, rainwater for the tea before the season; Golden seeds piled on the platter, frost-ripened tangerines.
The youth wanders aimlessly through the world; His body is covered in mist and water across a hundred southern cities.
As in the game of chess, worldly affairs are constantly renewed; cast off fame and office to cherish the True. A thousand-year-old crane comes to roam the Penglai Isles;
another spring has blossomed within the Peach Blossom Spring. The dark lute and yellow scrolls are my noble companions;
ancient rocks and tall pines serve as my neighbors. Cherish well you, the Master Xuan-yi of Panxi; at the hundred-foot height of the fishing pole, you know how to turn your body about.
A Reply in the Rhyme of Master Mengtang’s Letter Sent to Me (at the time of the re-editing of the *Sengzhuan*), Briefly Submitted by Ganlumei for the Revision of the *Sengshi*.
Yang Dainian pruned and compiled the *Chuan deng lu*; Yuan Miaojie of Youan Temple rejoiced anew in its restoration.
The true transmission of the successive patriarchs was widely propagated; The great Jambū tree provides cool shade to the entire world, Benefiting all sentient beings with patience.
How shameful for the immortals! The forests and groves throughout the four seas are overgrown with weeds. How can you bear to sleep in peace within these lofty halls?

I mourn that my Dharma-brother, the Venerable Nantang, preached the Dharma at a temple outside Lake Dongting. He returned once more to Zhiji to fulfill his auspicious prophecy; like clouds rushing and waters flowing, three thousand [disciples] gathered there.
The jade responds to the golden pestle throughout the twelve hours; the *śaṅkha* dragon returns to the bottomless bowl. The Vairambha wind shakes the branch that never sprouts.
East and west, this one who is both human and celestial has been lost; sentient and insentient beings alike knit their brows.
On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month in the Gui-mao year, the Nantang Hall collapsed against the Nirvana Platform. The Floating Banner King Realm appeared upon the tip of a single hair;
the Utpala flowers bloomed amidst the flames. Profound understanding and esoteric words were all swept away; true regulations and pure models were instantly restored.
Seven hundred li from Jiahe to Ning-shui, ears are turned to hear the thunder of the Dharma at all times.
Next, following the rhyme of Master Zhang of Zhongzhu, I present this verse to the attendant Ziji:
In our school there are no words and no dharmas; How could we permit reckless transcription or chaotic copying? Turning one’s head, the hordes of demons are all close attendants;
Raising one’s eyes, the thousand sages are not peers with whom to associate. The iron bowl that devours space—do not set a handle upon it; The golden boat that carries the moon—how well it sails!
Grasping the oar, he blew upon a tuft of cloth and suddenly attained awakening; clearly, he was merely tossing a lump of excrement at people.
In this same rhyme, I present this to the Japanese *zangchu* Jing:

running east and then west in search of the profound mystery, he seeks the sword by marking the boat, vainly remembering its traces. When the eyes are upright, dragons and snakes are fundamentally easy to distinguish.

In debate, his spirit soars above Buddhas and patriarchs as if swallowing them whole; he sweeps away the five thousand scrolls of the Tripitaka and brushes past the eighty-four thousand gates of worldly toil.
Ascending alone to the city tower, he gazes upon his native land: the cold sun over sea and heaven emerges like a golden basin.
Retiring from affairs beside the twin cypresses, I reply in the rhyme of Master Tianyuan’s nephew on the theme of "Living in Seclusion":
With four walls surrounding me, I am content with my lot; The sounding of the drum has no way to force me to attend the evening assembly. I leave it to the horn-call to reach my pillow;
Too weary to ask about the color of the grass south of the city wall. The iron ox’s lightning-eye cannot be caught by fragments; The stone maiden’s cloud-tresses are easily [disturbed].
Upon receiving the hairpin [of ordination], he recalled how Ciming had seen the divine cauldron; "With the rivers and streams as his tongue, to whom could he speak?
He inscribed this for Dajian An’s West Hall, following the two elders Xijiu and Guiyuan, and after Nantang, he once again brought forth one hundred ancient cases (gongan) selected by Xuedou.

A hundred chapters of ancient worthies’ leisurely koans; five-colored *maṇi* jewels illuminating the great thousandfold world. How many are amazed by the jade casket hidden within the forested clouds?
Yet more observe Xuedou striking the golden whip. From the Phoenix Terrace, light emits like the moon amidst the stars; from Mount Kunlun, fragrance drifts like lotuses within the fire.
Cherish the nimble hand of Nantang; now we meet Faxi, who follows in the footsteps of former sages.
Master Jidengtang (then at Daci Temple) dwelt in leisure at Lake Temple, discussing the illness of Chan.
It was as if he were back among the piled-up greens in Jiangxi: frost-covered creepers lean against the wall like the shed bones of dragons;

wearing his worn dharma robe over his shoulders, he walks along ant-tracks. Within his phrases, he conceals the blade-point, fully wielding both killing and giving life; had he lost his illumination even a moment before the pivot, he would have been cut off.
Clouds and mud. The Sovereign of Emptiness has endured from vast eons until this day; his great transformation is impartial, bringing all things to equality.
Composing these verses in rhyme to present to the Abbot Mìcáng of Línghyǐn:

Before the black staff is even raised, one knows where it will fall; it is not in vain that you rely upon me here on the western ancient cliff. It is rare to encounter one who can, with bare hands, tear open the shell of the dragon.
Nodding in agreement, he said: "Most often one seeks the tracks of a rabbit at withered stumps. Water can freeze into ice, yet ice is but water; mud can form an image, yet the image is not the mud.
Vairocana’s treasury of the ocean empties all existence; when for a single thought no arising occurs, ordinary and sage are equal."
A Verse on Rhyme to Show My Associates (II):
When great people gather to eat a stalk of congee, Do not speak of Zhaozhou’s “East of the Courtyard” or “West of the Courtyard. On the yellow-ash tree there is no honeyed fruit;
In the perilous place of the precipice, there is a level path. Shoulders bared, one has yet to bear a thousand-jin burden; Planting one's feet, one must first guard against the three [obstacles].
A foot of mud. The eye at the crown of the head of Mahesvara is vast and penetrating;
inferior forms and sublime marks are fundamentally equal. This mind has neither awakening nor delusion; yet for the most part, one travels east and ends up heading west.

If you believe the great void can be found with a seam, let the ancient path divide its own trails as it will. A swift thunderclap shatters a mountain like crumbling decay; a sharp sword strikes a bell as if striking wood.
Chenini. For me, an old man amidst mists and clouds, what use is there? The timing of Heaven and the affairs of men are indeed difficult to harmonize.

Answering the Heavenly King: On the Eastern Ridge, Elder Xun—clouds press down upon a thousand peaks, the path is about to be lost; snow leans against ancient cypresses by the broken bridge to the west. Prosperity and decay are self-evident, without the slightest [doubt].

Contemplation: Who would say there are two paths between clarity and obscurity? Guarding silence is the drowsiness of dull meditation, like oil soaking into flour; Seeking through texts is the madness of empty wisdom, like fluff clinging to mud.
An old man at twilight sings well the song of non-arising; He rejoices to see his grandsons singing it in perfect harmony.
I present this to the Japanese Zen Master Kenzō:
Your ancestral domain is so lofty and profound it has never been surpassed; you boast much of secret transmissions and direct inheritance. Yet the human mind is inherently devoid of past and present;

the fortune of the Dharma may indeed have its cycles of decline and rise. Cease wandering through a thousand gates with your iron bowl; raise it aloft amidst the empty embrace of the ten thousand phenomena.
Frosty vines—how unexpected that at dawn on Mount Bo-sang, one must rub one’s forehead in wonder! A flower blooms upon a withered tree in the ice of the sixth month.
To the storekeeper Xingwei and all teachers:
the treasury of luminosity is inherently present in every person; it is neither received nor transmitted from antiquity to the present. When it is easy to understand, do not strive to understand.
[The Master] replied: "Difficult places to seek are precisely where one should seek well. The ancestral lineage of Caoxi is called the Nanyue school; the descendants of Jicui yield to Jiyin.
Having received ordination from a master, you have returned to pay your respects; I still look forward to seeing you, Old Yunlin."

I bid farewell to the Elder Daji-pi as he departs for the realm of the Fragrant Ocean at Mount Potalaka, the King of Floating Banners. The gate of the ancient Buddhas’ perfect penetration stands wide open: verdant peaks rise loftily, piercing the azure heavens;
the whale-tossed waves roar like thunder in a clear sky. Like Muzhou of Mt. Miao who kicked over the pure pitcher, Huangbo took up the Chan staff.
The edition has arrived. A single phrase transcends the thousand sages; the atmosphere of the monastic groves is restored.

For the Elder Ding to travel and explore the profound mysteries, he must possess the eye. The patriarchs possessed profound mechanisms, yet one need only not follow their words, and in the end, one will be able to see one’s own mind.

It is difficult to fashion a mirror by polishing a brick; it is easy to turn iron into gold by alchemy. Regarding the stringless melody of the Primordial Age, we pledge to one another to bring forth its ultimate resonance.
Following the original rhyme, I remain on the road:

Master Zang’s devotion to the Ultimate Way is profound, while my concerns for this fleeting life are light. There is no separate method for action or withdrawal; both speech and silence are entirely true expression.

When the cataracts are cleared, the void is primordially pure; when the dust is dissipated, the mirror shines of itself. The wind and light overflow the eyes with clarity—where could one ask for the path home?
The Master Shangren sent his disciple Canfang to request words of parting.
Unfolding the paper, I again fell into deep reflection: the opinions of the current age are shallow and limited, while the minds of the ancient sages were vast and magnanimous.
Flawless, it is called a fine jade; extracted from the mine, it is refined gold. The Way is not obtained from others; seek it with single-minded sincerity.

In the same rhyme, lamenting the late Abbot Zao, a man of noble intent who sought the profound mystery: Master Lan’an of Oxherding. When the sentiments of sage and ordinary are exhausted, the ocean of birth and death can be dried up.
The *juésù* phoenix merely displays its auspiciousness; the *bājiāo* plant cannot endure the cold. A hundred years are truly but a single dream; all matters are entrusted to three sighs.
In the Jihai year of the Zhizheng era, I retired from affairs at Zhushan and returned to Yuanming Hermitage.
There, while reading the records of Master Zhenjing, I encountered these lines: "This one body has its ultimate limit; the myriad affairs have no end. I analyzed their meaning...
With the "Ten Cuts" as the preface, ten chapters of miscellaneous verses are composed.

To the left and right, a single hermitage neighbors a wooden well; this aged self is fit to retire from the world. Stones are piled to form a lotus pond, and a window is opened facing a medicinal railing.
Chaotic peaks rise steep and green; secluded ravines pour forth murmuring streams. There exists a life apart from the world; it is well to play the stringless lute.
Dwelling amidst a thousand ridges, how many times have the seasons changed? A staff overhanging the wall leans against it; a broken-legged cauldron is buried in the hearth.
A coarse cloth robe to ward off the cold, and old mugwort soup to satisfy the belly. Where the path turns and the stream winds back, who is it that comes to walk with me?
All day long I lean against the edge of a cliff; idle clouds depart and then return. If one does not realize that the mind is itself the Buddha, it is in vain to say the mirror is not the stand.
When turbid water is clear, the pearl reveals itself; in the mud, the lotus may be planted. In our school, there are many divergent views;

though one has a mouth, it is too weary to open. Having a body entails burdens; being without [the entanglements of] women is to be without seeking. One who can penetrate things as they arise—who among them would not be free?
The peanut grows because the eyes are obscured; one stays on the bank to moor the boat. The Way of the Dharma is ever transcendent and supreme; the Jetavana Garden is already in late autumn.

Within the fixed time, one ascends to the fruits of sainthood; yet, out of a particular stubbornness of mind, one clings to ignorance. A mere snap of the fingers spans three *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas; a single upraised glance covers a journey of a hundred thousand leagues.
Stone oxen plow the vast wilderness; straw dogs bark at the empty city. In the place where the truth is truly proclaimed, weeds grow thick before the hall.
Since when have the myriad dharmas ever existed? The single mind is fundamentally non-existent. Empty space is never destroyed; how many times has the blue sea dried up?
The old man of Vaiśālī possessed wondrous eloquence; the blue-eyed barbarian transmitted the single dharma. Strange that the wooden xiezhai deer has swallowed the stone *yitu*;
when principle and fact are already perfectly fused, what prevents one from discussing this school? All that is gathered is medicine; though held aloft, it does not become a dragon.
The grass before Mount Yangguang; the pines atop Vajra Ridge. How vast within this world of heaven and earth! For a thousand ages, one admires these numinous traces.
Ultimately, they cannot be transmitted; why then do you call them "Chan"? Manifesting the faculty is not within the words; grasping the intent is surely prior to speech.

A single shout distinguishes guest from host; at the tip of the staff, the orthodox and the deviant are revealed. The ancestral fields and lands remain; give the water buffalo a good lash of the whip. There is no matter to contemplate;
pass the years and seasons according to conditions. A precious duck sits upon the desk; a *kundika* hangs in the corner by the wall.

The rain has ceased, yet the sound of the stream remains powerful; the moon rises high, and the shadows of the pines linger. Within both emptiness and wondrous existence, each and every thing is known through penetrating insight.

Time and light have their pasts and presents, but the Buddha-nature is neither awakened nor deluded. What difference is there in the names used to express the Dharma? When returning to the source, the principle is naturally equal.

Directly teaching one to distinguish water from milk, yet inevitably remaining separated by clouds and mud. Forty-nine instances in a single stroke: Zhaozhou’s “East of the Courtyard” or “West of the Courtyard.
Following the rhyme of Chan Master Suan’s *Shouzuo*:

(2) Accomplishing a noble seclusion wherever one is, the divine pearl shines with a brilliant light through the night. Though the thatched hut is exceptionally cramped, the entire Dharma-realm is contained within it.

The imperial carriage with its curved wheels summons me from the capital; deep within the incense burner, the scent of yam fire rises. When epilepsy follows delusion and confusion, how could one not conceal the divine remedy?
When the Buddha of Awakening points his finger, the Ocean-Seal naturally emits light. Fire does not emerge from within a mirror; the pearl is not hidden inside a garment.
Porcelain bowls float with snowy milk; stone chambers are filled with celestial fragrance. Wondrously attaining the principle of true emptiness, the compass and square are naturally square and round.

Reading the ancients and examining the intentions of the former sages, there is not the slightest deviation. If the cataracts before one’s eyes have not been cleared, how can the flowers in the sky be removed?
A cool breeze arises upon the mats; the white moon shines through the window-silk. Closing the scroll, I sit in stillness; how can true contemplation have any limit?
In response to the verse sent by Master Pingshi of Tiantong (V):
He would not dwell aloft in Tuṣita Heaven; whenever he met someone, he sought but a single coin. He further spoke of Maitreya as the true Maitreya...
Heh! He scatters earth and flings sand before a hundred-fold assembly;
his Chan is like quicksilver in a crucible. When Huanglong heard of him, he immediately grew angry.
Had it not been for Old Ciming at that time, even an iron net could not have captured this one-horned qilin.
The three-foot bamboo whisk is always held in his grasp; he would never treat the Buddha-dharma as mere worldly sentiment.
Sitting loftily within the Snow-Illuminating Pavilion, he causes the eyes of the patch-robed monks to become clear for themselves.

Within the verdant mists of the sandalwood pavilion, an old man with white hair gazes upon the world with a heart like a clear mirror. As the incense in the stone cauldron has burned out, he first rises from his meditative concentration;
the golden sun beats its wings at the eastern gate of the sea.
Every head and every thing is entirely the true nature; who says that people today are ashamed of those of antiquity? Did Nanda ever follow after sense-faculties and consciousness?
Gautama merely tied his own flowered turban.
The rector sent to collect rice returns instead with charcoal; the duties of the Hall Superintendent thus trouble him at every turn.
To understand the meaning of the Western Come, it lies solely within the midst of ordinary daily life.

To the Monk Xi of the West, who came to inquire about the meaning of our Western Patriarch: In old age, one has a mouth that is best left idle. Zhaozhou once pointed to the cypress tree in front of the courtyard;
For a thousand ages, it has served as the core of discourse for the monastic community.
Bestowed upon Guest Master Jing:
Whether moving or still, cold or warm, you should know this for yourself. You have rushed through the waves of Jianghuai, Min, and Zhe;
now, as Guest Master at Dayang Monastery, you shall be a teacher for a hundred generations atop Niusou Peak.
Ten Poems on Antiquity Sent to the Great Master Xitang:
His tattered robes, patched a hundred times, barely cover his shins; Amidst a heap of dung-fire lies a yam tuber.
He never minds the cold tears falling down his chin, For a letter from the Nine Heavens has arrived upon purple clay.
It is not difficult to speak; it is difficult to recognize the truth. When Linji set out for Mount Jing with his bundle on his back, you should ask him yourself what was lacking.
In that hall of cloud-like companions, half had already left their mats.
Three or five pecks of green ash upon his head—whom would say Zhaozhou was too lax and idle?
If you casually raise your eyebrows to look, he is a tiger; the striped one is a great beast.
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, they do not strive for much; they do not walk where the Tathāgata walks.
It is no wonder that in years past, the eccentric Puhua kicked over the rice table and acted so crudely.
In the past, Baiyun saw Yangqi, who asked about his former teacher at Chaling.
"If he were not a true scion of the house, how could a single smile resolve his doubts?"
After Ciming finished his visit to Old Fenyang, he left with short hair and a shoulder-slung basket of antiques. When Shending saw him, old and dim-witted, they spoke;
most in the monastic forests have misinterpreted their discussion.
In the spring of the Bārajā Hermitage, the Great Way is vast; when Zen students come to inquire, there is no talk other than this. He directly reveals the extraordinary matter of Fenzhou:
unbinding the heart, shaking off the tattered robe.
The ancient masters showed people this plain proclamation: it is easy to look at, but difficult to understand.
Had it not been for those two turning words that hit the mark, how could Chuang-tzu have enabled Chia-shan?

In discourse with others, there is no obstruction; within one's own house, there is nothing, yet one brandishes weapons. From the outset, those of a certain sort have their deluded minds extinguished;
in the field where Buddhas are chosen, they attain the highest rank.

The three supervisors direct the yellow-toothed orifice toward heaven; the patch-robed monks have missed it by thousands upon thousands. When a document is copied three times, "wu" becomes "an," and "ma" becomes "ya.
Layering the subtle and doubling the profound, they vie with one another to speak of Chan.
Next, the rhymed verses of Master Liaohan (8):
The profound compassion of our Patriarch is not easily measured; He sought to become a great tree to provide shade and coolness.
Behold, after the five-leaf flower has bloomed, How could the myriad purples and thousands of reds dare vie for its fragrance?
The Hu monk arrived specifically, his golden staff flying through the air; he once caused the night assembly at Fenyang to be canceled.
He was not permitted to enjoy the leisure and stillness of Nantang, for he intended to propagate the Way of the Dharma throughout the southeast.
Not a single speck of dust remains; ten thousand conditions are empty. At midnight, the sun rises red from the bottom of the sea. The golden-haired lion emerging from its cave seeks no companion;
the fragrant elephant crossing the river—whom else could it share its path?
With birth and death, the source of the mind is muddled; without sagehood or ordinariness, the ground of nature is level. When guests arrive, do not resent my excessive neglect;
white clouds and flowing water naturally welcome and see them off.
With empty hands, one must probe for ice within the flames; do not seek other occupations for your own livelihood.
Where Deshan brandishes his white staff horizontally, that is the lamp of wisdom in the dark alleys of the world.
In every encounter and every circumstance, there is no dharma remaining; why must one necessarily penetrate that which has not yet arisen? This winter I rejoice in having firewood;
for now, I shall simply lower my curtain to preserve the warm smoke.

Kneading sand will never form a ball; the story of severing the arm to find peace is complete. To truly uphold and propagate the matters of the religious teachings—how could it be limited to the depths of grass before the Dharma Hall?
What is seen by the eye and heard by the ear has no separate essence. Grasping a black staff, he walks and then leans upon it; neither Bodhisattvas nor Śrāvakas have ever known this.
Each has realized one of the twenty-five perfect penetrations.
Xin’an said:
"Just this state of being without doubt is entering the gate; within it lies a separate heaven and earth. Why trouble yourself raising your fist toward a guest?
Day after day, white clouds hang from the thatched eaves."

At Tiantong Monastery in Taizhou, the Administrator (Duguan) molds an image of Guanyin; the Guest Prefect (Zhike) builds a pavilion for the monks to shave their heads and offers straw sandals as an offering.
Guanyin manifests in the body of a bhikṣu; the gates of the pavilion open to welcome those seeking the essential ford. Having shaved their heads, they eat their fill of radiant light.
Rice. Wearing double-layered straw sandals, whom do you see?
Entrust yourself to Master Juexue of Ziyuan;
do not disdain this desolate ancient site of practice. In our school, we value only the practice of the *huatou*. Zhaozhou once resided at Guanyin.
In the monastery, with wheat vinegar, sand, salt, and earth for a bed, he shows the Zen guests:
"If you come to ask, you must mute your mouth; if you go to answer, I must shave my tongue. The pillar in front of the hall laughs aloud.
Mei: When Bodhidharma came from the West, there was no secret formula.

Xuedou’s verse on the reversal of delusion and awakening is like falling plum rain drenching the perilous heights; one clear phrase cuts off both love and hate. Master Mo, the number of monks is small.
It is well. Most people take their intellectual understanding to be the true vehicle of our school.
In the mountain hermitage, the air is as cold as ice in the fifth month; I do not allow the wooden door to be opened easily.
A white mold has long since formed upon my lips, and I am glad indeed that there are no monks coming to inquire about the Dharma.
Do not say that Heaven and Earth have violated their great trust; from antiquity to the present, they have never differed by so much as a hair’s breadth.
Even Zhaozhou still possesses such earnest compassion that he would call out to every monk who came, "Come, have some tea."
Not yet having clarified the mind-ground is like a stifling heat; even if you have already clarified it, how can you find peace? You have planted a winter melon and are trying to grow eggplants;
a single hundred-patch robe will never be finished mending.
In response to Master Zhiquan of Lingyin:
The True Eye of Mahesvara illuminates heaven and earth; a Zen elder of the sixth generation from Wuzhuo; holding his bamboo whisk upside down, he fully manifests killing and giving life;
right before one's eyes, he shatters the Iron Kunlun.
The three stupas stand;
north of the pond, south of the stream, the grass is lush and green. Beating the bricks and striking the tiles, one sees the completion of the work.
One is not three, and three are not one. Which of those skulls lacks eyes?
The Bodhisattva Huadingguang fashioned a paper shrine atop the incense burner.

To ward off the cold while sitting in meditation, he crafted a garment from wild ivy to resist the chill. When the six directions are empty and luminous as he arises from samādhi, one realizes that although Zao Bo composed treatises in his time, he never knew the story told by the hearthfire.
Deep in the mountain retreats, yellow tubers are simmered in the hearth; in the bubbling cauldrons, bracken and ferns are boiled. What has not changed for kalpas past is the same as today’s affairs;
this year’s hunger is no different from last year’s.
By the banks of the Lùluó Creek, I open my thatched gate. I myself wash my tattered cotton robe and hempen cassock. The dry magpies call out, then call again;
after many years by rivers and seas, an old friend has returned.

Seeking the profound and searching for the subtle, all is in a state of confusion; who can turn the light back to investigate the original source? When the deluded views of all sentient beings across the great earth are dissolved, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, from the beginning, remained silent.
The Dharma community declines and my heart grows cold; all conditions are empty and still—what more can be said? Having awakened from sleep at the mountain window, the sun stands high at noon;
a single tree of *śāla* flowers is in full bloom.
The flat surface resembles a bed beneath the pines; the drooping branches form a canopy beside the rocks where the pines stand. For the mindless wayfarer, his eyebrows are like snow;
having brewed the tea, its fragrance is exceptionally rich.
Clouds have vanished from the shaded cliffs and the chill of winter arrives early; I gather the withered branches into two or three piles.
I do not let the vegetable leaves drift away with the current, fearing they might obstruct the arrival of a noble seeker of the Way.
Emerging from my thatched cave in stillness, I wander alone; unaware that the seasons of human life have changed.
I casually cast vine seeds into the clear pool, where countless fish vie for them upon the surface of the water.
Three logs of firewood smoldering, perfectly warm; three poles of cold sun, yet still sleeping high. Though one clearly knows there is a mouth, it may as well hang on the wall;
the myriad phenomena of the universe speak Chan in its stead.
Always born with this one body from one’s mother; let it be rich or let it be poor. Sitting upon a stone bed under the moon of the third watch, the wind lifts the pine waves that fill the ears.

The mountain peaks are so high that snow accumulates as soon as it grows cold; throughout the three winters, there are rarely times when it does not snow. Recalling the Second Patriarch, who stood waist-deep in snow before his master’s courtyard;
thinking of Yangqi, who shrank his neck while sitting upon his bed.
Inscription for the Portrait of the Patriarchal Assembly:
The Sages and Worthies Manifesting Their Auspicious Power in the World. How could a subtle brush capture them all completely?
Fortunately, there is the ancient broken "string of beads" (the nose-rope), which pierces their nostrils all at once.
In my solitary hermitage, I have built nothing more than a single thatched hut; even the jade palaces and pearl towers cannot compare to it.
Not only is it difficult for others to dwell with me there, but there is no one at all who can serve as a neighbor.
Encourage my nephew Zhongshi to travel to visit the various holy sites and seek the single patch of cloth upon the crown of all sages; do not decline the journey, for its length must be resolved.
Xueqiao returned to Touzi three times; Cimeng changed his robes to see Fenyang.

In this letter to the Sangha, I take the four sutras—*Śūraṅgama*, *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, *Samantabhadra-bodhicitta-uttaratantra*, and *Avataṃsaka*—directly from the flower-scarf to form six knots. By bending down to accord with the capacities of beings, I expound the Three Vehicles;
yet it is as if one has deeply entered the Treasury of Radiance, where by breaking open a single mote of dust, the Great Sutra emerges.
A Gift for Venerable Xian, Who Sought Donations for the Lotus Sutra Assembly: The sea embankment at Naih tang rises;
the staff-head reveals its true place. East, west, south, and north—moving freely in all directions. The assembly on Vulture Peak remains as if present before our eyes.
How many times have the tides of the blue seas and the fields of mulberry changed?
Lamenting the Venerable Yuzhong:

Among the long-established masters of all quarters, those of great virtue have almost entirely passed away. Now that Yuzhong the Elder has died at Huiyin, the decline and chill of the Dharma path can be clearly foretold.
Who shall succeed to the exemplary conduct and lofty spirit?
Sudden awakening to the heart-source empties all dharmas; he was especially devoted to esoteric practices to transform humans and devas.
With a hundred and eight beads in his hand, he causes them to blossom as golden lotuses amidst the fire.
Without doubt, why bother with divination east or west? Having long since possessed self-confidence, there has never been anything hidden.
Once this matter is seen with intimacy, dressing and eating are just as they always were.
In Memoriam of My Dharma Brother Bieyuan Shouchang (IV) Throughout his life, he was accustomed to employing the "Black Bean" method;
a true bone-son of the fifth generation of Songyuan. With confident steps, he trampled across the sea of birth and death;
with a direct pointing, he revealed the Iron Kunlun.
There is a mouth that does not swallow the Buddhas of the three periods; it wanders freely through the lands of the ten directions. When death arrives, one falls into the usual state of delusion;
the śarīra relics, a labor for men, fill a handful as they are gathered.
If the mind harbors sacred interpretations, the Way remains distant; though the medicine possesses divine power, the illness cannot be cured. Let the kalpa-fire burn the bottom of the sea as it may;
nirvana and birth-and-death are fundamentally suchness.
Separated by water and land for over a thousand li, brothers have not beheld each other’s countenance for ten years. His final message arrived yesterday at Zituo Temple;
his remains are already interred on Mount Danxia.
Guoqing requested bamboo from Tianfeng to make water conduits;

when asked lightly at the Double Streams Facing the Sun, Tianfeng responded directly below. Together they took up the intent of the hundred-foot pole, reaching the upper stream over a precipice of ten thousand fathoms.
Six Poems in Reply to My Dharma Brother Qingliang Shilian (Written at Taibai Peak) The Golden World is the Land of Coolness;
His boundless tongue unfolds in vast discourse. Before Taibai Peak, he shares half his seat— As upright as the Ling Tree awaiting Shao Yang.
Secluded in my thatched-roof hut, all worldly thoughts have turned to ash. How many times has the bright moon come before my window? Yesterday a monk departed for Mount Tai;
today he returns with a letter from Mount Luofu.
I know that grasping an elephant and grasping a rabbit require the same degree of effort; one must apply oneself with full diligence. Daily activities manifest with vivid clarity;
from the beginning, there has been neither attainment nor transmission.
Those whose faculties are not yet clear should refrain from harshness; for now, let us arrange matters beneath the bright window. At the sound of a single cry, the dog and wolf flee in haste;
outside the gate, the purple lake stands empty with its signboard.
The extraordinary matters of the Great and Small Yunmen have never contained a single dharma that can satisfy the mind.
When asked where the Buddhas emerge from, he simply said: "On the mountain waters of Dongshan."

I do not envy those who transcend their lineage or possess extraordinary talent; what need is there for extensive learning or vast knowledge? Having come in vain through the three thousandfold world-systems of the Buddha-lands, I have merely allowed myself to pass through the twelve periods of the human day.
Lamenting the passing of Master Juexue of Ziyuan, who in his later years retired to the summit of Thousand Peaks: His exhortations to awaken those yet unenlightened never ceased.
Hearing that he has departed through transformation this autumn, who will now once more raise the ox over the window?
The Dharma Master of the Stains holds a celestial youth;
wielding a pure broom, he comes forth to grasp an iron shovel. On the side of purity lies the achievement of merit, while on the side of defilement one cultivates practice.
With a chamber-stick, he sweeps out the Treasury of Radiance, causing the celestial youth and Old Xizhou to fall over in laughter.
How truly extraordinary and authentic! This old Chan monk does not realize his own tongue has grown long.
Having swept away five thousand scrolls of the scriptural teachings, he raises himself up from amidst a heap of dung.
Shi Lang’s attendant said:
"The wild duck flies clearly past; Master Ma pulls it back by the nose. The disciple merely strikes the icy bone with an iron pestle;
the flower blooms upon the branch that never sprouts."
The practitioner, with his merit as adornment, returns to bury his parents;
for those who are not kin, who is most kin? To repay their kindness, one must be the very person who owes them that debt.
Buried alive in yellow earth three feet deep, the flower blooms at the pestle’s tip—a spring beyond the kalpas.
Lamenting the Late Master Qingliang Songyin (II):
At eighty-five, his lifelong endeavors were complete; Sitting cross-legged with palms joined, he manifested his true return. The cremation left those present in profound amazement;
A chaotic rain of heavenly flowers and snowflakes flew down.
A direct descendant of the fourth generation of Xiqiu, he rides an iron horse backward up Mount Kunlun.
Among the myriad bodhisattvas on Mount Qingliang, one more image is added within the formless light.
Attendant Ni returned to visit Master Songgang:
The three thousand worlds of the ocean of lands manifest wondrous function; The eighty-four thousand afflictions reveal numinous knowledge.
At the place where Niaoke blew up the cloth-hair, And when Puhua performed his somersaults, All was overturned.
Sending off Elder Xiesheng Yan to reside at the Temple by the Side of the Immortal Nun’s Cliff in Wenzhou:

There, leaning his black staff across his lap, he will receive the stream of Chan practitioners; Like Master Hui’an, he shall break through and read the verses of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, Until even Mount Sumeru laughs and nods its head in approval.
The Patriarchal Lineage cast an iron net before the peak of Shaoshi; those who shake it forth are all jade-like qilins.
Since the five branches first diverged, how many have held it with their bare hands?
Next, Miscellaneous Verses on Mountain Dwelling by the Venerable Master Sōngam Sojung (4):
The Bodhisattva’s perfect cultivation brings him close to the Buddha; He withdraws from the three realms to rescue the orphaned and the poor.
Those who struggle blindly for power and race toward their goals— On their heads they wear a scorched bell weighing ten thousand jin.
Pressing down upon the cloud-head, one guards empty awareness; sitting facing a grain basket, one willingly accepts hunger. With cassia oars and orchid boat, one boasts of being a skilled hand;
yet it is not heard that the silken prize has been won and brought home.
A single phrase, clearly realized, transcends ten billion worlds. What more is there to doubt that you would wait for further instruction?
It is strange how in the past, my short junior uncle used to prostrate himself beneath Dongshan’s bed to listen.
Returning from the rivers and seas, my teeth and hair have grown thin; I have moved a single hermitage into the deep clouds to dwell. Herds of monkeys pluck sour pears;
when they see people, they scurry up the trees on the precipice.
A Four-Part Verse on the True Calligraphy of the Ancestor Tianmu Baoyue, in the Rhyme of Master Xiangshan Tang:

At the Foot-Washing Pavilion, he lavishly added to the cost and labor of the project. The skillful is revealed precisely within the clumsy. The mountain stream reveals his spiritual power as he washes his feet.
Different. At that time, amidst the turbidity, there was clarity.

Five hundred Arhats and five hundred Śrāvakas came to receive their predictions at Stone Bridge. Their supernatural powers moved like wind and thunder across their palms and faces; they could step upon the Stone Bridge or not step upon it.
Severance! For now, seek shelter within the stillness of deep clouds.
At Ruiyan, the alert stone is a strange stone;
at Pota, the yielding moss and lichen remain. The old Chan master sits precariously, neither leaning nor collapsing. For years he has proclaimed: "Alert! "Alert!"
[He] clings [to it]. Which one can emerge from its sphere of activity?
At Longqiu, Venerable Ju-na sat with his knees drawn up on an ancient cliff. Ten thousand bushels of views topple before the *śarīra*. I wish to deal him a severe blow.
In his hand. Alas, what can be done when he refuses to turn his head?
The "Table of Contents for the Orthodox Lineage of the Dharma Transmission of the Patriarchs" is like golden hammering meeting jade resonance;
the wedge drives out the wedge. The flame continues the fragrant succession; the mind-seal seals the mind. Within the realm of true purity, there is no fixed position.
Next: "There is one who understands above Jambudvīpa.
[The Master] replied, "To transmit the head seat (the position of the *śrāmaṇera*).
(2) Fenyang had a saying: "Do not engage in false imaginings. Changqing followed up, saying, "That too is quite mistaken. He kicked over the rice table and sent Pudu flying.
Transformation! As for the old Xuan Sha who built the foot-stool, his exhaustive mastery of worldly pivot-points is surely laughable; even exhausting all profound dialectics is likewise in vain.
Old Lu of the millhouse could not recognize a single character, yet it was he who transmitted the robe through the six generations.
Inviting National Master Qing’s Eastern Seat, Venerable Mukan:
when skin and flesh have fallen away, only the reality remains. With a single heart of emptiness, the water-mirror opens wide. It is just right to join Qingshang and Huikong in their wild devotion;
O ancient Buddha of Xizhou, we look for you to return.
Moved by the Cuckoo’s Call: Sent to Master Liaokong of the Eastern Seat at Guoqing Temple Counting back from now, I reckon my old friends;
Letters and news are blocked everywhere by wind and dust. The cuckoo cries atop the moon of the third watch;
I am but a single person, aged and ill, in this empty mountain.
I recall my late Dharma brother Qingying Zhong of Mingqing;
his voice and countenance have been separated from me by half a thousand li. That the leaves turn yellow has already startled me for thirty autumns.
There is nothing to be said regarding the subtle and great Dharma-gate; yet Qinshan had words to awaken Yantou.
I have divided the old composition into four chapters.
It shows how the *raṅka* (mendicant) Venerable Wei transformed rice upon returning, yet it was transformed back into charcoal. It is a sword that kills, yet a blade that gives life.
Who knows that where great kindness is difficult to repay, the ocean is not deep enough and the mountains are not high enough?
I have suddenly troubled you with the post of Hall Attendant. For one whose very bones are as cold as ice, the broken buckets and basins are bound together;
his two eyes are a piercing azure, and the black-spotted calico cat’s face is marked upon his forehead.
One must clearly understand the meaning of Xilai; though the throat is choked, one must still breathe. The Wordless Child recites Mahā;
Śākyamuni did not receive the prediction from Dīpaṃkara.

It occurs only within the midst of ordinary daily life; one must know that face-to-face, there are a thousand mountains between us. Though there is an eye within the phrase, it is ultimately difficult to comprehend;
yet upon the zither with no strings, it is precisely right to play.
Sending off a Monk Carrying His Alms Bowl:
The Awakened Sovereign alone is honored as supreme throughout the three realms; The propagation of the Dharma transformation rests with his descendants.
Joyfully beholding the cloud-like hall accommodating the ocean of the assembly, He holds aloft the iron bowl toward the gates of the donors.
It is well that this deaf old man was born with two ears that hear nothing; in old age, hearing is gone and ten thousand thoughts have ceased.
Whenever I see those beside me opening their mouths in laughter, I look up at heaven and idly twirl my white beard.
Having retired from public affairs at Taibai, I happened to read the records of Master Dongshi.
Among them was a verse by He Nengren congratulating Zhongnan upon his retirement from the East Hall. I divided it into four stanzas and showed them to those around me:
"Occupying the highest floor of the mountain stream cottage, I reflect that I come here barefoot, treading on the edges of ice. Even if one were to bestow a thousand pieces of gold upon me,"
Priceless. Throughout my life, I have been incapable of a hundred things;
having cast aside a whole hall of monks in the mountains, they shall all continue the ancestral lamp in years to come.
The myriad phenomena roar their teaching—why must I trouble myself to raise my staff?
The small garden has been moved beneath the balustrades; at the corner of the house, the wind from heaven rings out like iron horses.
Now that Liang-sui does not come to seek instruction, for whom does Magu hold his hoe?
I pluck wild *qí* greens myself and steam them with various grains; having eaten my fill, a lingering fragrance remains in every pore.
I laugh at that old man of Vaiśālī in days of yore, who expounded the Tathāgata’s Supreme Vehicle.

When bestowing a prediction of longevity or brevity, prosperity or decline, what need is there to speculate? It is determined at the very moment of that first cry upon the earth. O Master, you possess a wondrous tongue for discoursing on the heavens;
one’s own natal destiny and primal source should be known by oneself.

The tailor Shen Shi seeks no other method than the guiding thread and the needle; whether measuring long or comparing short depends on the occasion. Through pure mastery of craft, he gains self-insight;
his skillful and extraordinary technique is known by all.
The shoe-repairer Mr.
Bao sought out the broken wooden bed; buried beneath the dust for a long time, it was now restored by a master hand.
The First Patriarch personally carried it back to India, where Dayang transmitted it to continue the lineage.
Two thousand years after the passing of Kāśyapa, at the end of the Dharma, when *uṣṇīṣa* flowers bloom everywhere in spring, Kaśyapa alone has attained the True Dharma Eye,
rendering the hundreds of thousands of people on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa as nothing more than a delusion.
Six Poems on the Same Rhyme:

Miscellaneous Remarks from Leisurely Dwelling A solitary, withered vine leans against the edge of the emerald pool; Gazing at my reflection, I am startled to find both temples already autumnal. The ancestral Way flows through and fills the seas and lands;
Old Master Lu, carrying his grain-mortar, has emerged from Xinzhou.
Having a mouth, why trouble yourself to raise the "head of the phrase"? Wansong’s voice shakes the autumn of the four seasons.
Standing in formation outside the bright moonlight, how strange was Old Xizhou back in his day!
Striking out the qilin staff from its head—its function like a flash of lightning, its spirit sweeping across autumn.
Urging Linji to study under Huangbo; such thoroughgoing maternal compassion is Muzhou’s.
The turning of the body depends on a single hair’s breadth; it is as solemn as a divine mountain in the autumn of the blue sea. Fu the Elder has lost his eyes;
the sound of the horn has blown through the ancient Yangzhou.
The cowherd is skilled at pulling the rope from the head; the ancestral fields will surely yield their autumn harvest. One does not see Mount Gui transmitting to the son of Ji;
the Great Dharma of the Lineage is flourishing in Yuanzhou.
A single room in an empty mountain, its white peaks reaching their end; throughout the Jeta Grove, there is nowhere autumn does not wither. How easy is it to bind one's waist and follow Yàojião?
Even more difficult is it to emulate Zhàozhōu’s practice of traveling on foot.

Lamenting Master Xuanyi’s burial beneath the plains, where grasses and trees now grow wild; yet Master Xuanyi has never truly perished. His legacy is transmitted through the *Qīngliáng zhuan* and the *Bōtuó zhuan*, leaving a brilliant radiance upon these famous mountains for a thousand ages.
